> (T6 · social maneuver) *She writes a note to Octavia — three lines, no more: the loyalty, placed; Thursday; unfazed.* — remembered: *Three lines, no more.*
> (T7 · look closer) *The note goes by first post in the morning. The sealing is quick. The weeks have taught her quickness.* — remembered: *She has learned quickness.*
> (T8 · choice) *The lamp is put out in the hall. The house takes its night shape. The eve is banked.* — remembered: *She lets the house sleep.*
> *(The night closes with the loyalty placed and the eve banked — the shape chosen, the road walked — and Rose stands at the window with the whole weight of Thursday in the placed loyalty: the sittings, the commission, or the plain word. The studio opens tomorrow. The town will be watching. The week turns with the loyalty kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the wreck week's ritual — dress for the studio and for public loyalty; direction + twenty 5-coin pins, story morsels between, reveal coda. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "London, Thursday. Miss Hartwell will be seen at Mrs. Wren's studio daily, in the full view of the ton, and at the tables of the week besides. The dress code of the wreck week: armor — but the visor up. The gown must stand beside a besieged friend without hiding her and without performing her. **Editorial criterion: loyalty, worn openly.**"
>
> **A. The Rampart** — crimson silk, martial; the stand, stated. Motif: the Hartwell oak in gold thread at the shoulder — the house, declared. Thread: **gold** (the loyalty, stated) / **copper** (warmth for the week) / **crimson silk** (the loyalty, matched). Colorway: crimson + gold + cream. Accessories: the gold oak brooch; her grandmother's pearls; violets at the wrist, faithfulness.
> **B. The Aegis** — deep blue silk, steadiness for the week; the shield, worn. Motif: the oak worked small at the hem in silver — the house, restrained. Thread: **silver** (the loyalty, edged) / **steel silk** (the loyalty, matched) / **blue whitework** (the loyalty, lit). Colorway: deep blue + silver + pearl. Accessories: the silver ribbon at the throat; pearl drop earrings; violets at the wrist, faithfulness.
> **C. The Redoubt** — black silk, severe; the dress of gravity. Motif: the oak in jet at the shoulder, dark on dark — stitched to be watched. Thread: **jet** (the loyalty, edged) / **black silk** (the loyalty, matched) / **grey whitework** (the loyalty, lit). Colorway: black + jet + pearl. Accessories: the black ribbon; a single pearl pin; violets at the wrist, faithfulness.
>
> *(The dressing room, the hour of the sitting: armor of the week for the studio — the martial, the stated, the hers. She dresses the way the week has dressed her: to stand beside a friend without hiding her.)*
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *She commits: the Rampart, the Aegis, or the Redoubt — the thesis of the wreck week, remembered. The hair, composed. The accessories, exact. The mirror, to be consulted briefly. **Direction.** London, Thursday — the studio, the sittings, the town watching. Dress to stand beside a besieged painter. **Editorial criterion.** Loyalty, worn openly — every choice must show the eyes, not the shadow of the armor.*
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the sittings. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins — 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins; no Crown SKUs; jewels from owned pieces only, never a ritual step.)*
> **Pin 1 (T2 · micro-decision) — Gown, chosen:** the face of the week — the crimson stated, the blue steady, or the black grave — whichever the week chose, the loyalty worn. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 (T3 · micro-decision) — Fit, exact:** composed — no rustle for the hush of the studio, no train for the judgment of the town. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 (T4 · micro-decision) — Sleeves, long:** for the sitting — composed, unhurried, giving the whisperers nothing. *5 coins.*
> *(The pins accumulate — the line of the gown set, the sleeves of the week — and the dressing room holds its candlelight the way the workroom holds its chalk: patiently. Élise pins the hem herself and says, "The visor up, Rose. They must see your eyes. The armor is for the week. The eyes are for her.")*
> **Pin 4 (T5 · micro-decision) — Neckline, open:** the visor — the throat uncovered, the face unshadowed; the town reads openness first. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — Hair, coiled:** braided — composed and kept; no ornament. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — Ribbon, at the throat:** the punctuation of the direction — gold, silver, or black — the loyalty, tied. *5 coins.*
> *(The ribbon tied — the knot of loyalty — and the morning leans in, the hour of the sitting waiting. In the corner of the workroom, half-seen behind the dress forms, an older woman folds tissue — grey hair, quick hands, gone before Rose looks twice. Élise does not introduce her. Rose does not ask.)*
> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — Gloves, removed for the sitting:** courtesy to the painter — the hands bare for the holding of the pose; the town can read the bareness. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T9 · micro-decision) — Slippers, quiet:** of the stairs — the stair of the studio, unheard. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — Fan, carried:** the companion of the reticule — the punctuation of the sitting, unopened. *5 coins.*
> *(Quiet slippers, the weight of the fan — the sitting asks for quiet, and she gives it.)*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — Brooch, the oak:** of the direction — gold, silver, or jet — the small heraldry, pinned at the shoulder. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — Scent, none:** for the sitting — no perfume for the air of the studio; the town smells the loyalty, not the lady. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — Posture, straight:** of the sitter — held and offered; the answer of the spine to the easel. *5 coins.*
> *(The spine straightens — offered and held — and the mirror is consulted briefly from the corner of her eye. Violets at the wrist, faithfulness, pinned small where only she will know them.)*
> **Pin 13 (T14 · micro-decision) — Gaze, level:** of the sitting — met eye to eye, Octavia's. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T15 · micro-decision) — Voice, measured:** of the week — the matrons count the words; measured is serious. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T16 · micro-decision) — Hands, still:** of the pose — held, composed; the bareness shown. *5 coins.*
> *(Level gaze, measured voice, still hands — the instruments of the sitting, tuned for the light of the studio.)*
> **Pin 16 (T17 · micro-decision) — Step, measured:** of the stairs — of Thursday, descended. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T18 · micro-decision) — Smile, worn:** of the week — the open, the unhidden; the whole meaning of the visor. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T19 · micro-decision) — Pearls, her grandmother's:** at the throat — continuity, worn; Hartwell continuity, stated. *5 coins.*
> *(The pearls at the throat — the continuity, stated — and the candlelight of the dressing room does its final work. The gown is armor. The face is unshadowed. No one will mistake the week for anything but hers.)*
> **Pin 19 (T20 · micro-decision) — Reticule, weighted:** of the week — the memorandum book within, the pencil, the exact; and folded small beside them, the miniature page — the truth, carried. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T21 · micro-decision) — The door, faced:** the last pin is not a pin — it is the turning toward the stairs, the face of the week set, the loyalty worn whole. *5 coins.*
> *(The reveal: the stairs descended, the door of the hall opened, the carriage waiting — the wreck week, dressed. The gown is the answer of the week before the painter lifts her pencil: loyalty, worn openly. The coda of the ritual is not a mirror. It is the door of the studio, ahead — the sittings, the town watching, the friend within — and the stand, worn like the gown: armor, the visor up, hers.)*

ritual.occasionBrief: Monday to Sunday; the wreck; the stand; the turn.
steps: Pin 7: Gloves, removed for the sitting:

scenes.synopsis: Thursday morning — Rose comes to the studio first and sits where the town can see; the siege meets the stand. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Thursday morning, ten o'clock. The studio door stands open on the mews, and the north light lies across the floorboards in clean slabs. The chairs are set in their row — the empty chairs of the headaches and the postponements — and Rose comes up the stair in Élise's armor with the visor up, on the dot of the hour, where the whole street can watch her climb.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *She counts the curtains that twitch on the way up: three. A carriage slows at the corner and does not stop. The town is taking attendance.* — remembered: *She counts the curtains.*
> (T2 · stance) *She takes the first chair — the chair of the countess, the one with the headache — and sits in it squarely, in full view of the door. The stand, worn.* — remembered: *She takes the first chair.*
> (T3 · dialogue) *"You are early, Miss Hartwell." Octavia's voice has its exact edge. "The sitting is at eleven." "I am the audience, Octavia. Audiences arrive early."* — remembered: *She arrives early.*
> (T4 · tone) *Light — "If the Lash wants to watch a woman sit in a chair, let it. Chairs are not libel." A breath of laugh from the workroom, quickly tidied.* — remembered: *She keeps it light.*
> (T5 · social maneuver) *She asks for tea to be brought for two, and asks it of the girl loudly enough for the stair to hear. The household will report a sitting in progress.* — remembered: *Tea for two.*
> (T6 · examine) *The easel stands ready, the canvas primed. Octavia's pencils are laid in their row, each one exact. The precision is up like a barricade — Rose alone can see what it costs to keep it there.* — remembered: *She sees the cost.*
> (T7 · dialogue) *"Then we begin at eleven, painter." "We begin at eleven, Miss Hartwell." The formality is the tenderness, for now.* — remembered: *Eleven, then.*
> (T8 · remembered micro-decision) *She will come every day the studio is open. The town may read it as it likes. She has stopped minding the reading.* — remembered: *Daily, whatever they read.*
> *(The tea comes, and the girl sets it down with wide eyes, and the street below goes about its business a fraction too loudly. The first chair is filled. The siege has its answer, and the answer is sitting in it, drinking tea, in armor, with the visor up.)*

scenes.synopsis: Thursday — Rose doubles the portrait commission before a witness and says it where the town will hear; the stand is priced in the open. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Thursday, past eleven. Letitia arrives with her workbasket and her spectacles and no intention of painting anything, and Rose waits until the girl has gone down for more hot water before she says it — clearly, for the room, for the stair, for the street with its twitching curtains.)*
> (T1 · stance) *"Octavia. The portrait commission — I am doubling it." Said aloud, no hedging, the words set down like a hand of cards.* — remembered: *Said aloud.*
> (T2 · dialogue) *"Rose —" "Call it arithmetic, painter. You have lost two countesses and a bishop's widow. I have not lost a thing, and I intend to keep it that way."* — remembered: *Arithmetic, not charity.*
> (T3 · tone) *Letitia, threading a needle she does not need: "Doubled. I shall tell everyone at whist tonight. The town loves a sum it can repeat."* — remembered: *Whist will hear it.*
> (T4 · look closer) *Octavia's pencil stops mid-row. The precision holds — barely. "You will be called extravagant." "I am extravagant. It is my best-known feature."* — remembered: *Extravagant, then.*
> (T5 · social maneuver) *Rose writes the memorandum in her book, then and there, and reads it back: the commission doubled, the sittings daily. Letitia signs as witness with a flourish.* — remembered: *Written and witnessed.*
> (T6 · dialogue) *"The Lash will call it a purchased defense." Octavia, exact. "Let it. The Lash calls everything something. It called your husband a fraud on Monday."* — remembered: *Let it call.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *She will not halve it, will not soften it, will not do it quietly. The doubling is the point. Let it be public.* — remembered: *Public is the point.*
> (T8 · choice) *"Thursday, painter. We have a portrait to paint, and the town has a lesson to learn. They are the same lesson."* — remembered: *One lesson.*
> *(The girl comes back with the water and hears the tail of it, and by Thursday evening the mews knows, and by Friday the town: the commission doubled, said aloud, witnessed. The matrons will have their word for it. Rose has hers first.)*

scenes.synopsis: Thursday afternoon — Letitia holds the studio door with wit; the audience stays respectable and the town cannot misread it. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Thursday afternoon. Letitia establishes herself by the studio door with her mending and her spectacles and the air of a woman holding a fortress gate, and turns away nobody — which is the point, because nobody comes, and the turning-away would be the story.)*
> (T1 · tone) *"No, dear, the painter is engaged. Yes, engaged in being painted at. It is the new fashion. You should try it — sitting still improves the complexion."* — remembered: *She turns away nobody.*
> (T2 · dialogue) *"Aunt." Rose, low. "There is no one there." "There might be. Hope is a discipline, darling. I am disciplined."* — remembered: *Hope is a discipline.*
> (T3 · look closer) *Two ladies cross the street rather than pass the door. Letitia notes their bonnets in her book, the way other women note sermons.* — remembered: *She notes the bonnets.*
> (T4 · stance) *She sends the girl down with a tray for the cabmen waiting at the corner — tea, bread, cheese. The cabmen will talk, and their talk is better than the clubs'.* — remembered: *Tea for the cabmen.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *She will sit at this door every day of the siege. Somebody must mind the threshold, and she minds things beautifully.* — remembered: *She minds the threshold.*
> (T6 · tone) *"If the Lash wants a headline — 'Dowager's Niece Holds Door; Door Unmoved.' I shall write it myself."* — remembered: *She writes her own headline.*
> (T7 · dialogue) *"You are enjoying this." "Darling, I am forty-something and invisible. Enjoyment is all I have left. Guard the painter."* — remembered: *She enjoys it.*
> *(By evening the cabmen have told three streets that the Hartwell ladies are holding the studio like a garrison, and the story is funny, and funny travels faster than libel. The door is held. The town cannot misread a joke — though heaven knows it will try.)*

scenes.synopsis: Thursday evening — Augusta prices the social cost; a dinner list closes and Rose loses standing with the matrons. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Thursday evening. Augusta's drawing room, the fire lit against a thin rain. The old lady reads the week the way she reads everything — once, completely, and without moving her mouth — and sets down her spectacles when she is done.)*
> (T1 · dialogue) *"Lady Castlereagh's dinner, Saturday. You are not on the list, child. The list went out this morning."* — remembered: *Saturday closes.*
> (T2 · tone) *Dry — "I sent my acceptance a fortnight ago." "And this morning it was un-sent. The matrons have excellent handwriting, when they wish to be rude."* — remembered: *Un-sent.*
> (T3 · look closer) *Augusta turns the note over. The paper is good. The cut is direct. No excuse offered — which is the whole shape of the insult, and Augusta admires the shape while condemning the manners.* — remembered: *No excuse offered.*
> (T4 · stance) *"I shall not dine at Lady Castlereagh's on Saturday." Rose, level. "I shall sit in a painter's studio and be doubled in oils. The menu is better."* — remembered: *She dines with the painter.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"Two more lists will follow. The musical evening, the card party. By Sunday you will be dining with your aunt and your grandmother, like a schoolgirl in disgrace."* — remembered: *Two more lists.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *Augusta will not intervene. Intervention would mark it as a campaign; silence marks it as weather. She chooses weather.* — remembered: *She chooses weather.*
> (T7 · tone) *"The matrons are pricing you, child. It is their trade. You are overpaying, in their coin — which is exactly why I am proud of you, and exactly why I shall not say so where they can hear."* — remembered: *Overpaying, in their coin.*
> (T8 · choice) *"Then I am priced." Rose stands. "Tell Lady Castlereagh I am engaged on Saturday. It will be true. I am engaged to a portrait."* — remembered: *Engaged to a portrait.*
> *(The rain goes on, and the fire burns down, and the ledger of the matrons grows by one line: Hartwell, R. — stands by the painter; priced accordingly. Augusta writes nothing down. She does not need to. She has priced granddaughters before.)*

scenes.synopsis: Thursday — the first quiet sitting; Octavia draws Rose, and the drawing is the truth-telling. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Thursday, the hour of the sitting. The studio settles — Letitia at the door, the girl banished to the stair, the north light doing its honest work — and Octavia lifts her pencil, and the room goes quiet in the particular way of rooms where something is about to be true.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *She does not pose Rose like a sitter. She looks at her the way she looked at the miniature page — the long look, the one that finds the person under the posture.* — remembered: *Held under the long look.*
> (T2 · stance) *Rose sits as she is: the armor, the visor up, the hands still. No smile arranged. "Draw me as I am, Octavia. The town can have the rest."* — remembered: *As I am.*
> (T3 · dialogue) *"The town has never had you, Rose. It has had your bonnets." The pencil moves. "Hold still. Thinking is allowed. Fidgeting is not."* — remembered: *Thinking allowed.*
> (T4 · tone) *Quiet, from the easel — "You doubled the commission where the stair could hear." "The stair has excellent hearing." "The stair will gossip." "The stair is my publisher now."* — remembered: *Published by the stair.*
> (T5 · examine) *The drawing comes up fast: the line of the jaw, the set of the shoulders, the eyes looking straight out. No flattery in it. Octavia does not flatter; she witnesses.* — remembered: *She witnesses.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *Rose will sit every day. Not for the town, not for the Lash — for the pencil, which is the only honest press in London.* — remembered: *For the pencil.*
> (T7 · dialogue) *"It is good." Rose, looking at the first study. "It is you." Octavia, not looking up. "Whether it is good is for the town. That it is you is for me."* — remembered: *It is you.*
> (T8 · choice) *She asks for the study when it is done — the first truth, before the portrait. Octavia gives it. Some things are not for the town.* — remembered: *She keeps the study.*
> *(The light fails at four, and the pencil stops, and the first sitting ends the way true things end: without ceremony. The study goes into Rose's book, between the memorandum and the miniature page. Two truths, drawn. The town has its libel. Rose has her likenesses.)*

scenes.synopsis: Friday — the Lash answers the stand; Bell lays the sheets of the week side by side and the rhyming shows. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Friday morning. The Lash answers Thursday: a paragraph on the doubled commission, a wink at the open studio door, the wreck retold with the varnish fresh. And Bell comes with the sheets of the week folded under her arm and a face like a woman who has done her sums.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *She lays three sheets on the table — the Lash, the gossip column of the Chronicle, the society page of the evening paper. The paragraphs rhyme. Not the words — the shape of them.* — remembered: *She lays out three sheets.*
> (T2 · dialogue) *"Read the third lines." Bell, soft-voiced. "The wreck, the widow, the friend. Three papers, one paragraph, three mornings running. Gossip does not keep time like that."* — remembered: *Gossip keeps no time.*
> (T3 · examine) *Rose reads. The phrasing differs; the order does not. The widow first, the friend second, the taint third — a liturgy, printed in three fonts.* — remembered: *One liturgy, three fonts.*
> (T4 · tone) *Dry — "Somebody is writing the rhymes, Mrs. Bell." "Somebody is paying for the rhymes, Miss Hartwell. Writing is cheap. Printing three papers is not."* — remembered: *Printing is not cheap.*
> (T5 · stance) *"Print it." "I print what I can prove." Bell folds the sheets. "I can prove the rhyme. I cannot prove the hand. The Gazette will note the pattern and name no one."* — remembered: *Pattern noted; none named.*
> (T6 · dialogue) *"And the doubled commission?" "The town will call it purchased." Bell, blunt. "The Gazette will call it a commission. Doubled. Witnessed. That is what I can prove."* — remembered: *A commission, doubled.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *Rose will bring Bell every sheet of the week, dated and kept. Somebody is keeping the archive; it may as well be her.* — remembered: *She keeps the archive.*
> (T8 · choice) *"The war is turning, Mrs. Bell." "Wars turn, Miss Hartwell. Papers print. Bring me Thursday's sheets."* — remembered: *Bring Thursday's sheets.*
> *(Bell goes with the sheets under her arm, and Rose stands at the window with the week in formation: three papers, one paragraph, three mornings. Somebody writes the rhymes. Somebody pays for the printing. The defense has its first map of the attack.)*

scenes.synopsis: Friday — Julian is seen at the studio; the wall holds in public; yellow roses come again. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Friday afternoon. Julian comes to the studio at the hour when the street is busiest, in his best coat, with a book he does not open — and sits in the second chair, squarely, where the curtains can count him.)*
> (T1 · dialogue) *"The prodigal returns." Rose, from her chair. "I was never lost, Rose. I was merely unpublished."* — remembered: *Unpublished, not lost.*
> (T2 · tone) *He looks at the empty chairs. "Two countesses and a bishop's widow. The studio is quieter than my club, and my club is a tomb."* — remembered: *Quieter than the club.*
> (T3 · look closer) *He sits through the whole sitting, turning pages he is not reading, a young lord with nothing to do but be seen doing it. The curtains twitch in rhythm.* — remembered: *He sits through it.*
> (T4 · stance) *"They will say you are besotted." "They have said worse, and in better print." He turns a page. "Let them spell it correctly."* — remembered: *Let them spell it.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"Octavia." He rises when the light fails. "The portrait will be magnificent. I know nothing about painting, which has never stopped me having opinions."* — remembered: *Opinions, uninformed.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *Octavia bows — precisely, the exact depth — and Rose sees the barricade lower one notch. The wall has four stones now, and one of them is laughing.* — remembered: *One notch lower.*
> (T7 · choice) *"Come tomorrow, Julian." "I shall. I have nothing else to do, and doing it here annoys the right people."* — remembered: *He will come tomorrow.*
> (T8 · tone) *At home, the hall table: yellow roses, another dozen, no card. The fourth week running. Rose looks at them a long moment, then tells the footman the kitchen may have these too.* — remembered: *Downstairs again.*
> *(The roses go downstairs, and the studio keeps its Friday, and the wall stands where the town can count its stones: the painter, the patron, the aunt at the door, the young lord with his unread book. Somebody's handwriting, in flowers, keeps arriving. The kitchen is becoming a bower.)*

scenes.synopsis: Friday evening — the matrons' ledger grows; two more lists close and Rose counts the cost of the stand. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Friday evening. The letters come with the last post: the musical evening, the card party — both lists made, both without her. Augusta predicted two. Augusta is never wrong about lists.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *Rose holds the two notes to the light, as if thin paper might show a thinner excuse. It does not. The cut is direct, twice over.* — remembered: *Twice direct.*
> (T2 · dialogue) *"The musical evening." Letitia peers. "I played badly at it for twenty years. You are well out of it, darling."* — remembered: *Well out of it.*
> (T3 · tone) *"And the card party?" "Mrs. Althorpe cheats at whist. Everyone knows. You are better out of that too."* — remembered: *Better out of that.*
> (T4 · stance) *"It is three lists in two days, Aunt." The levity costs her something; Letitia hears the cost and does not name it.* — remembered: *Three lists, two days.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *Letitia will write to Mrs. Althorpe about the whist cheating — not now, later, when it will sting most. Some revenges are best served cold, and hers are arctic.* — remembered: *Arctic revenge, later.*
> (T6 · dialogue) *"The town is pricing me." "The town is pricing your loyalty, darling, and finding it expensive. That is not an insult. That is a valuation."* — remembered: *A valuation.*
> (T7 · choice) *Rose puts the notes in the drawer with the sheets of the Lash. The archive grows: libel, lists, roses. The week is keeping its own accounts.* — remembered: *Filed with the libel.*
> *(Letitia goes home to her cold revenge, and Rose sits with the accounts of the week: the studio filling, the lists emptying, the roses arriving, the sheets rhyming. The matrons have priced her. The price is public. She finds, to her surprise, that she can afford it.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE COMMISSION: the doubled commission needs a public form that does not diminish Octavia; Rose chooses its shape. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Friday night. The memorandum book lies open: the commission doubled, witnessed, waiting for its shape. Money is blunt, and Octavia is proud, and the town is watching — and the form of the thing is the thing. The lamp burns. The week waits.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — The commission:*
> - **A second portrait** — *Commission a companion piece: Augusta has offered to sit. Octavia becomes a painter in demand, not a charity case.* (Consequence: Augusta's terms are absolute — the sittings will be ordeals, the portrait a public verdict, and Augusta does not sit for painters she does not respect.)
> - **The exhibition** — *Announce the Rose portrait for the spring exhibition of the Academy. The commission becomes a career, not a kindness.* (Consequence: the establishment that cooled must be faced head-on — and if the town hisses the picture, the hiss lands on Octavia.)
> - **The plain sum** — *Double the money on the existing portrait, stated plainly, no second picture, no dressing. Honest patronage, honestly named.* (Consequence: the town will call it a purchased defense, and Octavia — proud, precise Octavia — may read the money as pity, whatever Rose intends.)
> - (T1) **Choose** — *the second portrait, the exhibition, or the plain sum. The shape of the money is the shape of the respect.*
> - (T2) **Remembered consequence** — *whichever form it takes, the town will name it first and unkindly; Rose's naming must be faster and truer.*
> - (T3) **The road** — *the chosen form, carried into Saturday; the commission made public in its shape, not just its sum.*
> *(The book closes on the decision. The money has its shape now — the respect, given form. Tomorrow the town hears it. Tonight the lamp goes out on a week that has learned how to spend.)*

scenes.synopsis: Friday night, late — the chosen form of the commission is carried to Octavia; the pride of the painter is the stakes. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Friday night, late. Rose goes to the mews herself, past the hour for calls, with the memorandum book and the decision in it — because some things must be carried by hand, and this is one.)*
> (T1 · stance) *She lays the book open on the worktable: the commission, doubled, in its chosen form — the second portrait, the exhibition, or the plain sum, whichever she chose. "Read it, Octavia. It is yours to refuse."* — remembered: *Yours to refuse.*
> (T2 · dialogue) *Octavia reads — precisely, twice. "You give me the refusal." "I give you everything, painter. The refusal is the least of it."* — remembered: *Read twice.*
> (T3 · look closer) *The precision holds. Then, for the first time all week, it does something else: it softens, at the corners, the way ice softens before it bears weight.* — remembered: *Softening at the corners.*
> (T4 · tone) *"The town will talk." "The town talks. It talked on Monday about your husband. It will talk on Saturday about your portraits. Talk is weather."* — remembered: *Talk is weather.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *Octavia does not refuse. She turns the page, takes up her pencil, and writes her acceptance under Rose's memorandum — in her own hand, her own terms.* — remembered: *Her own terms.*
> (T6 · dialogue) *"The sittings continue." "The sittings continue." "The town watches." "Let it watch. It will see a painter working, which is more than it usually sees."* — remembered: *A painter working.*
> (T7 · choice) *Rose leaves the book with her — the memorandum, the acceptance, the doubled sum in its shape. The commission belongs to them both now.* — remembered: *Belongs to both.*
> (T8 · look closer) *On the stair down, she hears the pencil resume upstairs — the small, sure sound of work going on after hours. The week has its music.* — remembered: *Work goes on.*
> *(The mews is dark, and the workroom burns its one light, and the commission stands in its chosen form — accepted, in Octavia's own hand, on Octavia's own terms. The money has been given its shape, and the shape is respect. The town may name it what it likes. The painter has named it first.)*

scenes.synopsis: Saturday — callers come to the studio and Rose tells the ton plainly that she chooses her friends. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Saturday afternoon. Curiosity brings them — the town cannot resist a siege with good lighting — and the studio fills with callers who have no intention of sitting for anything. Rose receives them in the armor, the visor up, with Octavia's pencil going steady behind her.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *She counts the bonnets: eleven. Three are friendly, four are curious, four are here to report back. She smiles at all eleven identically.* — remembered: *Eleven bonnets.*
> (T2 · dialogue) *"Miss Hartwell." Mrs. Althorpe, sweet as arsenic. "We had hoped to see you at the musical evening." "I was engaged, Mrs. Althorpe. To a portrait."* — remembered: *Engaged to a portrait.*
> (T3 · stance) *She does not apologize, does not explain, does not soften it. She stands beside the easel and lets the town look at the stand it has been pricing all week.* — remembered: *No apology.*
> (T4 · tone) *"You choose your friends remarkably, my dear." "I choose them, Mrs. Althorpe. Remarkably or not, the choosing is mine."* — remembered: *Mine, the choosing.*
> (T5 · social maneuver) *She says it for the room, not the woman: "I choose my friends, and I stand by them where the town can see. The town may make what it likes of that. It usually does."* — remembered: *Said for the room.*
> (T6 · dialogue) *A silence — the particular silence of eleven bonnets recalculating. Then one of the friendly three laughs, and the tension breaks the way ice breaks: all at once.* — remembered: *Ice breaks.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *Octavia's pencil never stops. Rose hears it behind her, steady as a pulse, and stands a fraction straighter for the sound.* — remembered: *Steadied by the pencil.*
> (T8 · choice) *The callers go, and the reports go with them, and by Saturday evening the town has the plain word verbatim: she chooses her friends. The matrons will price that too.* — remembered: *Out goes the word.*
> *(The studio empties, and the north light slants, and Octavia sets down her pencil and looks at Rose for a long moment — the long look, the one from the miniature page. "Well," the painter says, "you have told them." "I have told them," Rose says. The plain word stands.)*

scenes.synopsis: Saturday — Cecilia comes with pressure dressed as concern; wealthy, connected, untouchable; Rose does not bend. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Saturday, past five. The callers gone, the light failing — and Cecilia comes up the stair like she owns it, in silk the color of money, with the yellow roses' perfume going ahead of her. She has not knocked. She never knocks.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *She looks at the studio — the easel, the empty chairs, the armor on Rose — and smiles the smile of a woman pricing a room she could buy twice over.* — remembered: *She prices the room.*
> (T2 · dialogue) *"Rose. Darling." The concern is beautifully done. "The town is saying such things. I came to see if you are — quite well."* — remembered: *Beautifully done.*
> (T3 · tone) *"I am quite well, Cecilia. The roses were lovely. The kitchen is enjoying them." A pause. "The kitchen sends its regards."* — remembered: *Regards from the kitchen.*
> (T4 · stance) *Cecilia's smile does not move. "You are ruining yourself for a painter, darling. The lists, the whispers. It is such a waste of a Hartwell."* — remembered: *Such a waste.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"Withdraw, Rose. Quietly. No one would blame you — the town forgets by Tuesday. I could help you forget. I have helped before."* — remembered: *Offer made.*
> (T6 · look closer) *The offer hangs there — the money behind it, the connection, the untouchable ease of a woman who has never been refused anything that mattered. Rose looks at it the way she looks at libel: steadily.* — remembered: *She looks steadily.*
> (T7 · choice) *"No." One word, level. "The painter is my friend, Cecilia. I choose my friends, and I stand by them. You heard me tell the town. I am telling you."* — remembered: *No.*
> (T8 · tone) *Cecilia rises, unhurried. "Pity. The town eats loyalty for breakfast, darling. I do hope you enjoy being the meal." The door closes softly. Untouchable, to the last.* — remembered: *Out, untouchable.*
> *(Rose stands in the empty studio with the perfume fading, and the pressure lifts off her shoulders like a hand removed. The offer was real — the money, the rescue, the forgetting. So is the refusal. The week has its line drawn, and the line is here.)*

scenes.synopsis: Saturday evening — Laurent and Henry are seen at the studio together; the town counts the stones of the wall. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Saturday evening. Laurent brings Henry — the Frenchman and the soldier, the laughed-at and the vindicated — and they take the third and fourth chairs like men taking positions, while the street performs its evening promenade below.)*
> (T1 · dialogue) *"Major." Laurent, expansive. "You have not seen the portrait." "I have seen the pencil at work, Comte. It is enough."* — remembered: *Enough.*
> (T2 · tone) *Henry looks at the canvas — the Rose coming up in oils, the visor up, the eyes straight out. "It is her," he says, plainly. "Paint her exactly like that, Mrs. Wren. It is the truth."* — remembered: *Plainly, the truth.*
> (T3 · look closer) *Laurent watches the street through the window, amused. "Three curtains, a carriage, and a matron with a quizzing glass. The town is doing its sums, chérie."* — remembered: *Summed by the town.*
> (T4 · stance) *"Let it." Rose does not look up from her book. "The sums come out the same every night. Four stones, one wall."* — remembered: *Four stones.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"The Lash will print us all." Laurent lifts his glass — he brought champagne, this time opened. "To the wall. May it bore the town into surrender."* — remembered: *To the wall.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *Henry drinks to it, and Laurent drinks to it, and Rose drinks to it, and the studio holds its Saturday evening like a small garrison holding a hill — cheerful, provisioned, unmoved.* — remembered: *They drink to the wall.*
> (T7 · tone) *"They cannot move us, you know." Julian, arriving late with his unread book. "We are furniture now. Very expensive furniture."* — remembered: *Furniture.*
> (T8 · choice) *The four of them sit while the light goes, and the town counts what it can see through the curtains: the painter, the patron, the Frenchman, the soldier, the young lord. Five, by one count. The wall does not care about arithmetic.* — remembered: *Five, by one count.*
> *(The champagne is finished, and the evening ends, and the wall stands counted by the curtains of the town: present, proven, unattacked, unmoved. Somebody is paying for the rhymes. The wall is not for sale.)*

scenes.synopsis: Saturday — Élise inspects the armor of the week and reports on the atelier; the town has been watching the gown. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Saturday morning, the atelier. Élise circles Rose with her pins and her critical eye, inspecting a week's campaign the way a general inspects a battlefield — and finds the armor holding.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *She checks every seam, every pin, the set of the shoulder. "It holds," she pronounces. "The week tried to wrinkle you, and the week failed."* — remembered: *It holds.*
> (T2 · dialogue) *"The week at the atelier?" "Orders, darling. Three new, all studio ladies. The town wants to dress like a siege."* — remembered: *Dress like a siege.*
> (T3 · tone) *"And the talk?" "The talk is that you are magnificent and ruined, in that order, depending on the street." Élise pins a loose thread. "The streets disagree. The atelier does not."* — remembered: *Streets disagree.*
> (T4 · stance) *She steps back, head tilted. "The visor stays up, Rose. It is the whole of the design. The moment it comes down, the town wins."* — remembered: *Visor up.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *Élise will make a second gown — the same armor, darkened for evening. The siege may run long; the wardrobe will keep pace.* — remembered: *A second gown.*
> (T6 · dialogue) *"You dress me for war, Élise." "I dress you for yourself, darling. The war is incidental."* — remembered: *Incidental war.*
> (T7 · choice) *Rose looks at herself in the glass — the martial line, the stated stand, the eyes showing. The town has watched this gown all week. Let it watch another.* — remembered: *Let it watch.*
> *(The atelier hums, and the pins fly, and the armor is inspected and found sound. The town has spent a week looking at Élise's work and calling it a statement. Élise calls it Tuesday. The visor stays up.)*

scenes.synopsis: Sunday morning — the second quiet scene; Rose and Octavia walk, and the devotion deepens without surrender. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday morning, early. The park is empty but for the birds and the distance, and the two women walk the long path the way they have walked it since spring — not hurried, not lingering, the pace of people who have nowhere to be but here.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *Octavia walks without her precision for once — the shoulders down a fraction, the step unmeasured. Rose has seen this walk twice before. She does not remark on it.* — remembered: *Unmeasured, for once.*
> (T2 · stance) *They do not talk of the Lash, the lists, the roses. They talk of the portrait — the line of the jaw, the trouble with the left hand, the north light failing at four.* — remembered: *That left hand.*
> (T3 · dialogue) *"You have lost dinners for me." Octavia, at the turn of the path. "I have gained a portrait." Rose, without stopping. "The arithmetic favors me."* — remembered: *Arithmetic favors her.*
> (T4 · tone) *"The town will not forget this week." "The town forgets everything, Octavia. It forgot the wreck for eleven years. It will forget my dinners by Tuesday."* — remembered: *By Tuesday.*
> (T5 · examine) *A silence walks with them a while — companionable, unforced. The devotion is in the pace, not the words: neither hurrying, neither holding back.* — remembered: *Pace held.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *Rose will not ask Octavia to soften, to hide, to be less precise for the comfort of the town. The precision is the person. She chose the person.* — remembered: *She chose the person.*
> (T7 · dialogue) *"The sittings continue." "The sittings continue." Said together, like a vow, like a joke, like both.* — remembered: *Like a vow.*
> (T8 · choice) *At the park gate they part — Octavia to the studio, Rose to Sunday's reckonings — and neither looks back, because neither needs to. The walk is the promise. It has always been the walk.* — remembered: *It has always been the walk.*
> *(The park empties behind them, and the week turns toward its last day with the heart of it intact: two women, one path, the devotion deepened and neither surrendered. The town has its libel and its lists. The walk has its walkers.)*

scenes.synopsis: Sunday — Octavia's precision cracks, once; Rose witnesses it and does not look away. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday afternoon. The studio is quiet — the town at its dinners, the street empty — and the portrait stands on the easel with Rose coming up in it, the visor up, the eyes straight out. Octavia works the background, precise as ever. Then the pencil stops.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The hand gives it away — the exact hand, the instrument — hovering over the canvas and not descending. A moment. Two.* — remembered: *Hovering, not descending.*
> (T2 · stance) *Rose does not move from her chair. She has learned when to be still: this is the time.* — remembered: *She is still.*
> (T3 · dialogue) *"I am afraid, Rose." Said plainly, without the edge, without the measure — three words, unprecise, the most inexact thing Octavia has said all week.* — remembered: *Three words.*
> (T4 · tone) *No wit, no deflection — Rose has none ready, and would not use it if she had. "I know," she says. It is enough.* — remembered: *Enough.*
> (T5 · examine) *The crack is one sentence long. Then the precision comes back — the shoulders square, the pencil descends, the exact edge returns like a tide.* — remembered: *Tide back in.*
> (T6 · dialogue) *"Forgive the interruption." Octavia, exact again. "There is no interruption, painter. There is only the sitting."* — remembered: *Only the sitting.*
> (T7 · remembered micro-decision) *Rose will never mention it — not to Letitia, not to Augusta, not to the book. Some things are witnessed, not recorded.* — remembered: *Witnessed, not recorded.*
> (T8 · choice) *The pencil goes on, and the portrait goes on, and the fear sits in the room like a third person — acknowledged, unhoused, outlasted.* — remembered: *Outlasted.*
> *(The light fails, and the sitting ends, and Octavia cleans her brushes with the usual exactness — every bristle, every ferrule. The crack was one sentence. The precision is the person. Rose saw the person, and the person saw her seeing, and the devotion deepened by exactly one sentence.)*

scenes.synopsis: Sunday — the second sitting of the weekend; the portrait advances; devotion without surrender, on both sides. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday, the evening sitting. The lamps are lit early against the dark, and the portrait has its second life under lamplight — warmer, less exact, more true, the way evening is truer than morning.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The Rose in oils looks back at Rose: the armor, the visor up, the eyes. Octavia has painted the stand without painting the defiance — the distinction is the whole of her genius.* — remembered: *Stand, not defiance.*
> (T2 · stance) *"You have made me kind." Rose, studying it. "I have made you visible." Octavia, not looking up. "Kindness was already there. I only paint what sits down."* — remembered: *Visible, not kind.*
> (T3 · dialogue) *"The town will see a Hartwell in armor." "The town will see what it sees. I paint the sitter. The town paints the story."* — remembered: *Two paintings.*
> (T4 · tone) *Quiet — "Will you varnish it, when it is done?" "I will varnish it, Rose. Varnish is patience made visible."* — remembered: *Patience, visible.*
> (T5 · examine) *They work past the hour — the pencil, the brush, the sitter holding still. The devotion is in the duration: neither asks the other to be less than she is.* — remembered: *In the duration.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *Octavia will not soften the portrait for the town, and Rose will not ask her to. The surrender is refused on both sides, like a toast.* — remembered: *No surrender, both sides.*
> (T7 · dialogue) *"It will be finished by spring." "Spring." Rose smiles. "The town will have forgotten the wreck by spring." "The town will have found a new wreck. There is always a wreck."* — remembered: *Always a wreck.*
> (T8 · choice) *Rose leaves by the mews door, the way she came all week — past the empty chairs, now less empty, past the easel with its true Rose. The week of the heart is nearly done.* — remembered: *By the mews door.*
> *(The lamps burn on after she goes — Octavia works late, the way she always has — and the portrait stands in the lamplight with its visor up. Devotion, deepened. Surrender, refused twice over. The heart holds.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE TURN: Rose holds proof of the coordination of the week; she chooses how the defense turns toward attack. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday night. The archive lies open: the sheets of the week, dated, the rhymes marked in blue pencil — three papers, one paragraph, three mornings. Somebody writes the rhymes. Somebody pays for the printing. The proof of the planting is here, in her hands. What she does with it is the turn.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — The turn:*
> - **Give it to Bell** — *Carry the dated sheets to the Gazette and let Bell print what she can prove. Principled, slow, and out of Rose's hands.* (Consequence: Bell will print the pattern and name no one — and she will print Rose's maneuvering too, if it becomes the story. The Gazette cuts both ways.)
> - **Name it to the ton** — *Carry the pattern into the drawing rooms herself and name it aloud: the rhyming sheets, the paid ink. Fast, public, and dangerous.* (Consequence: the town will listen — and the planters will hear her coming. Naming the pattern makes Rose the story, and the story can be libeled.)
> - **Hold it** — *Say nothing yet. File the proof, keep the archive, and let the planters print again — overplay needs rope.* (Consequence: patience is a weapon, but the next sheet may land harder than this week's. Holding the proof means holding the risk.)
> - (T1) **Choose** — *Bell, the ton, or the holding. The proof is the weapon; the hand that wields it is the choice.*
> - (T2) **Remembered consequence** — *whichever road, the money behind the ink stays hidden — the tracing comes later. This turn proves the planting, not the purse.*
> - (T3) **The road** — *the chosen road, walked Sunday night; the defense turns toward attack, in the manner Rose chose.*
> *(The archive closes on the decision. The proof has its road now — Bell's press, the ears of the ton, or the filed dark. The week began with the wreck in full. It ends with the planting proved. The war has turned.)*

scenes.synopsis: Sunday night — the chosen road is walked; the turn is carried in the manner Rose chose. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday night, late. The house is quiet, the week banked — and Rose walks the road she chose: the sheets to Bell, the pattern to the ton, or the proof filed for the overplay to come. The manner is hers. The turn is real.)*
> (T1 · stance) *She does it herself — no deputy, no letter, no whisper through a third party. The turn is hers, and she carries it in her own hands.* — remembered: *In her own hands.*
> (T2 · look closer) *The archive goes with her, or stays filed, or goes to the press — whichever she chose. The blue pencil marks hold: three papers, one paragraph, three mornings.* — remembered: *Marks holding.*
> (T3 · dialogue) *"It is done." She says it to the empty hall, trying the shape of it. The hall does not answer. The hall is discreet.* — remembered: *Discreet hall.*
> (T4 · tone) *Steady — the week has taught her steadiness the way the sea teaches swimming: by immersion, without lessons.* — remembered: *By immersion.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *She will not tell Octavia tonight. The painter has had her week; the turning of the war is Rose's to carry until morning.* — remembered: *Until morning.*
> (T6 · examine) *The memorandum book gets the line: the turn, taken. The means, remembered. The game of the week is written down.* — remembered: *Written down.*
> (T7 · choice) *She banks the lamp, the way she banked the eve on Wednesday. The house takes its night shape. The week is nearly done.* — remembered: *Lamp banked.*
> (T8 · look closer) *At the window, the mews dark, the one light of the studio burning. Octavia works late. The wall holds. The turn is walked.* — remembered: *Turn walked.*
> *(The night closes over the walked road — Bell's press, the ears of the ton, or the filed dark, whichever she chose — and the defense has become the attack in the manner of Rose Hartwell: personally, precisely, and without asking permission. The week has one hour left.)*

scenes.synopsis: Sunday — Bell verifies what she can; the Gazette prints the pattern, names no one, and may cut Rose too. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday, the Gazette office. Bell has the sheets of the week spread on her desk like a general's maps, and her soft voice has its hardest edge — the edge she uses when she is about to print something true.)*
> (T1 · examine) *She has checked the rhymes — the third lines, the order, the three mornings. "The pattern holds," she says. "I can prove the pattern. I print the pattern."* — remembered: *Pattern holds.*
> (T2 · dialogue) *"And the hand behind it?" "I cannot prove the hand." Bell, blunt. "Suspicion is not print, Miss Hartwell. You know my terms."* — remembered: *Her terms hold.*
> (T3 · tone) *"You will name no one." "I will name no one. The Gazette notes the coordination and lets the town do its own arithmetic. The town is good at arithmetic."* — remembered: *Town arithmetic.*
> (T4 · look closer) *She turns a sheet over. "And this — your doubled commission, your daily sittings, your plain word to eleven bonnets. If the planters answer, the Gazette prints that too. I cut both ways, Miss Hartwell."* — remembered: *Both ways.*
> (T5 · stance) *Rose meets the sharp eyes steadily. "I would not have you otherwise, Mrs. Bell." "Most people would. That is why most people are not worth printing."* — remembered: *Worth printing.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *Bell will run the pattern in Tuesday's Gazette — the rhyming sheets, the three mornings, the paid look of it. No names. The town will read between the lines; the town always does.* — remembered: *Tuesday's Gazette.*
> (T7 · dialogue) *"The money behind the ink —" "Is not proved." Bell folds the sheets. "When it is proved, I print it. Until then, it is your archive, not my paper."* — remembered: *Not yet proved.*
> (T8 · choice) *"Thank you, Mrs. Bell." "Do not thank me, Miss Hartwell. Read me Tuesday. And bring me next week's sheets."* — remembered: *Next week's sheets.*
> *(Rose leaves the office with the verdict of the week: the pattern proved and printed, the hand unproved and unnamed, the money still in the dark. Bell serves the truth, not Rose — and the truth, this week, is enough for the turning of the war. The rest comes later.)*

scenes.synopsis: Sunday evening — Augusta accounts the week; the cost is priced and the worth stated, dryly. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday evening. Augusta's drawing room, the fire high. The old lady has the accounts of the week in her head — she keeps them there, the way other women keep jewels — and lays them out for inspection.)*
> (T1 · dialogue) *"Three lists, child. The Castlereagh dinner, the musical evening, the Althorpe cards. Three closed doors."* — remembered: *Three closed doors.*
> (T2 · tone) *"And on the other side of the ledger?" Rose asks. "One painter, standing. One commission, doubled. One town, told." Augusta counts on her fingers. "The arithmetic is vulgar, but it favors you."* — remembered: *Vulgar arithmetic.*
> (T3 · look closer) *She pours the tea herself — a thing she does for no one, which is the whole of the benediction.* — remembered: *She pours herself.*
> (T4 · stance) *"The matrons will forgive you by spring. They always do — forgiveness is their cheapest coin, and they spend it freely on the young and well-dressed."* — remembered: *Cheapest coin.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"And if they do not?" "Then you will dine with me on Saturdays, like a schoolgirl in disgrace, and be better company than the matrons."* — remembered: *Better company.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *Augusta will write to Lady Castlereagh — not to plead, but to be seen writing. The town reads her pen the way it reads the Gazette.* — remembered: *Seen writing.*
> (T7 · tone) *"You chose your friend where the town could see, child. I have priced granddaughters for seventy years. You are the first I have not wanted to discount."* — remembered: *No discount.*
> (T8 · choice) *Rose kisses the old cheek — a thing she does rarely, which is the whole of the answer.* — remembered: *Answered with a kiss.*
> *(The fire burns down, and the price of the week stands accounted: three lists lost, one friend kept, one town told. Augusta sips her tea. The ledger balances — in her coin, which is the only coin that has ever mattered to Rose.)*

scenes.synopsis: Sunday — Élise delivers the second gown; the armor continues and the siege dresses on. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday afternoon, the atelier. The second gown stands on the form — the same armor, darkened for evening, the visor still up — and Élise fusses over it the way other women fuss over infants.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The silk is midnight now, the oak in silver, the line martial as ever. "For dinners you are not invited to," Élise says. "One must dress for the dinners one declines."* — remembered: *Dinners declined.*
> (T2 · dialogue) *"You think ahead, Élise." "I think in silk, darling. It amounts to the same thing."* — remembered: *Thinking in silk.*
> (T3 · tone) *"The town watched the first gown all week." "The town will watch this one longer. Dark silk photographs the resolve better."* — remembered: *Photographs resolve.*
> (T4 · stance) *She pins the shoulder herself, the small heraldry exact. "The visor stays up, Rose. Even at dinner. Especially at dinner."* — remembered: *Especially dinner.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *Élise will send the bill to no one — the gown is her stand, her stone in the wall. Artists have their own currency.* — remembered: *Her own currency.*
> (T6 · dialogue) *"You are in the wall too, Élise." "Darling, I built the wall. You are merely standing on it."* — remembered: *She built it.*
> (T7 · choice) *Rose wears the new gown home through the Sunday streets, and the town — what is left of it outdoors — turns to look. Let it. The armor holds.* — remembered: *Worn home.*
> *(The atelier door closes on the week, and the two gowns hang side by side — the armor of the week and of the next, the visor up on both. Élise pins a final thread and smiles. The siege dresses on.)*

scenes.synopsis: Sunday night — the household banks the week; the roses go to the kitchen and the archive closes. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday night. The house settles — the lamps banked, the books closed — and Letitia comes for the last tea of the week, with the last of the news and the first of the calm.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The hall table stands empty of roses for the first time in a month — the bower in the kitchen is now three weeks deep, and the servants' hall smells of a florist's.* — remembered: *Empty, at last.*
> (T2 · dialogue) *"The maids have started pressing them, darling. In books. Your siege is becoming a herbarium."* — remembered: *A herbarium.*
> (T3 · tone) *"Let them press." Rose smiles. "Somebody's jealousy, preserved for botany."* — remembered: *Preserved.*
> (T4 · stance) *The archive goes into the drawer — the sheets, the lists, the blue-penciled rhymes — and the drawer locks with a small, final click.* — remembered: *Locked.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *Letitia will keep her own copy of the sheets of the week — "for the memoirs, darling" — and Rose does not ask what memoirs.* — remembered: *For the memoirs.*
> (T6 · dialogue) *"You held the door all week, Aunt." "I held the door, darling. It is what aunts are for. That and the cold revenges."* — remembered: *Aunts' work.*
> (T7 · choice) *They drink the last tea in companionable quiet — the week banked, the heart intact, the wall standing.* — remembered: *Last tea.*
> (T8 · look closer) *At the stair, Letitia pauses. "Your painter is a lucky woman, Rose." "I am the lucky one, Aunt. Do not tell her. Her precision would not survive it."* — remembered: *Do not tell.*
> *(The house sleeps, and the week is banked — the sittings, the commission, the plain word, the turn. The archive waits in its drawer. The kitchen smells of roses. The heart holds.)*

scenes.synopsis: the Gazette sting — Bell prints the pattern of the week in her own blunt voice; one reading turn. (Turns: 1)
scenes.prose: > (T1 · the sting) *"On the sheets of the week. Three papers printed one paragraph on three mornings — the widow, the wreck, the friend, in that order, the phrasing different and the shape the same. Gossip does not keep time like that. Somebody paid for the timekeeping. The Gazette notes the pattern and names no one: the Gazette names only what it can prove. The proving continues. — N.B."* — remembered: *Bell prints the pattern.*
scenes.sting: On the sheets of the week. Three papers printed one paragraph on three mornings — the widow, the wreck, the friend, in that order, the phrasing different and the shape the same. Gossip does not keep time like that. Somebody paid for the timekeeping. The Gazette notes the pattern and names no one: the Gazette names only what it can prove. The proving continues. — N.B.

scenes.synopsis: Sunday night, late — the proof: the wreck story was planted and paid for; Rose knows the hand that paid for the ink. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday night, past eleven. A knock — a boy from the print shop, rain on his cap, with a parcel delivered wrong — proof sheets and a bill, made out for Miss Vane's lodgings and brought to Hartwell house by mistake. He apologizes. He is paid for his trouble. He goes.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The bill is from the printer of the Lash: the wreck sheets, Monday's full printing, composed and run — and across it, in a clerk's hand: paid in full.* — remembered: *Paid in full.*
> (T2 · examine) *Under the bill, the pulled proof of Monday's sheet — the wreck in full, the black letter — and a covering note, directing the placement: the widow first, the friend second, the taint third.* — remembered: *Placement directed.*
> (T3 · stance) *Rose reads the covering note twice. Then a third time, the way Octavia read the memorandum — precisely, completely.* — remembered: *Three readings.*
> (T4 · tone) *The handwriting is not a clerk's. It is a lady's hand — educated, unhurried, accustomed to being obeyed. Rose knows it the way she knows her own.* — remembered: *A lady's hand.*
> (T5 · dialogue) *"Cecilia." She says it to the empty room, quietly. The room does not answer. The note answers.* — remembered: *Answered by the note.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *She will not run to Bell tonight — the proof is hers until morning, and the morning is soon enough for the press. Tonight it is hers alone.* — remembered: *Hers until morning.*
> (T7 · choice) *She puts the bill and the proof and the note into the archive drawer, with the sheets of the week and the blue-penciled rhymes. The drawer locks. The proof is filed.* — remembered: *Filed.*
> (T8 · look closer) *She stands at the window with the last page of the week written: the wreck was planted, the planting was paid for — and the hand that paid for the ink is Cecilia's. She knows it. That is all. That is everything.* — remembered: *She knows the hand.*
> *(The lamp goes out. The house sleeps. The week of the heart closes with the recognition standing alone in the dark: Cecilia's hand paid for the ink. The money behind the hand — whose purse, whose orders — waits in the dark with it. That comes later. Tonight, the hand is known.)*

scenes.synopsis: Monday — Rose comes down to Hartwell Park; the grounds dressed for a thousand; the war moves to her earth. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Monday, past noon. The carriage turns in at the Park gates, and Hartwell Park comes up the drive the way it has come up all her life — the oaks, the lake lying flat as a coin, the house with its face to the weather — and this week it is wearing its war paint. The tents stand on the south lawn, white as sails. The kitchens are going up behind the east wing in timber and canvas. The flower carts wait on the gravel like a harvest come early.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The south lawn is a field of canvas: three great tents for the supper and the dancing, their guy-ropes staked in lines as straight as ledgers.* — remembered: *She counts the tents.*
> (T2 · examine) *The kitchens behind the east wing — a second kitchen, built for the week, with its own ovens and its chalk sums on the boards. A thousand guests eat a great deal. Somebody has done the arithmetic where the cooks can see it.* — remembered: *Chalk sums.*
> (T3 · look closer) *The lake, with the course marked round it in white posts. The water lies flat and takes no interest in wars.* — remembered: *No interest.*
> (T4 · tone) *Dry, to the coachman — "The Park is dressing for a siege." "A fête, miss." A pause. "The same thing. The same thing."* — remembered: *The same thing.*
> (T5 · stance) *She gets down at the steps and walks the gravel herself — the grounds she rebuilt across the seasons, stone by stone, now the war's set-piece.* — remembered: *She walks it.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *The memorandum book: Monday — the Park, the tents, the kitchens, the lake. The campaign's ground, surveyed.* — remembered: *Ground surveyed.*
> (T7 · choice) *She will walk every acre before the week is out. Her earth, her fête, her war — in that order, and the order matters.* — remembered: *Every acre.*
> *(The house takes her in, and the week takes its shape around her: the tents, the kitchens, the lake, the flowers by the wagonload still to come. She stands at the window of her own room with the Park spread below like a map she drew herself. The war has come to her ground. The ground is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: Monday — the morning room becomes the war office; Augusta absolute, Letitia funny; the preparations run like a campaign. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Monday afternoon. The morning room at the Park has become a war office: the long table buried in lists, the seating plans pinned to the boards, the flower orders in stacks. Augusta sits at the head of it like a general who has done this before — she has — and Letitia paces with a pencil behind her ear.)*
> "The lists, child." Augusta taps the paper. "A thousand guests. Four hundred chairs for the supper; the rest will stand or be lucky. The kitchens want the numbers by Thursday. The kitchens will have the numbers by Thursday." — Augusta
> (T1 · look closer) *The lists in Augusta's hand — columns, ticks, the marginalia of seventy years of fêtes. The old lady runs a campaign the way other women run a household: completely.* — remembered: *Completely.*
> (T2 · tone) *Letitia, pacing — "A thousand guests, darling. I have written a thousand names and I no longer believe in the alphabet."* — remembered: *The alphabet fails.*
> "The alphabet will recover, Aunt. It always does." — Rose
> (T3 · stance) *"The flower orders are the weak point." Augusta sets down the sheet. "Wagonloads, and every stem accounted for. Somebody's hand could turn a meaning in a garland and no one would know until the guests read it."* — remembered: *The weak point.*
> (T4 · dialogue) *"Then the flower room gets a guard, Grandmama."; "It gets you, child. You read flowers the way I read lists."; "Then it gets read daily."* — remembered: *Read daily.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *Rose takes the flower orders herself — the stacks, the chalk marks, the growers' names. The weak point becomes her point.* — remembered: *Her point now.*
> (T6 · tone) *"The stables, darling." Letitia stops pacing. "The pass. A thousand guests will want to see the Park's horses, and the Park's horses will want to see the thousand guests, and I foresee drama."* — remembered: *Drama foreseen.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *"The stables get Henry." Rose marks the list. "Soldiers understand horses and crowds. It is practically the same discipline."* — remembered: *Henry gets the stables.*
> (T8 · choice) *Augusta rises, and the war office rises with her — the campaign has its commanders, its weak point, its cavalry. The week begins in earnest.* — remembered: *Commanders set.*
> *(They go out with the lists divided — Augusta the guests, Letitia the alphabet, Rose the flowers and the horses — and the morning room settles into its new shape: headquarters. The fête is a campaign now. The campaign has begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: Monday evening — Julian, Laurent, Henry, and Octavia arrive at the Park; the household gathers for war. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Monday evening. They come down by the afternoon coaches and their own horses — Julian with his unread book, Laurent with champagne, Henry in uniform, Octavia with her sketchbook — and the hall fills the way it fills when the house is holding something. Rose receives them on the steps, and the receiving is the muster.)*
> "The garrison reports, Miss Hartwell." Julian bows. "I bring nothing useful and excellent morale." — Julian
> (T1 · tone) *Warm — "Morale is useful, Julian. The town says so. The town is occasionally right."* — remembered: *Occasionally right.*
> "Chérie." Laurent kisses her hand. "I bring champagne and a Frenchman's eye for ground. The fête will be magnificent. I have decided." — Laurent
> (T2 · dialogue) *"Decided, Laurent?"; "It is my gift, chérie. Decision, without evidence."; "A rare gift. Guard it."* — remembered: *Without evidence.*
> "Miss Hartwell." Henry salutes, exactly. "The stables are mine, I am told. I have walked them. The horses are good. The grooms are better." — Henry
> (T3 · stance) *"The pass is yours to stage, Henry. The grounds' own horses, a riding week inside the war."* — remembered: *His to stage.*
> "Rose." Octavia comes last, quiet. "I brought the sketchbook. Somebody should draw the Park before the thousand arrive, while it is still ours." — Octavia
> (T4 · look closer) *The sketchbook under her arm, the pencil behind her ear. The painter at the Park looks younger — or the Park looks kinder. Rose does not decide which.* — remembered: *Undecided.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *She gives them their stations the way Augusta gives orders: Julian the town's talk, Laurent the eye, Henry the horses, Octavia the record. The garrison is posted.* — remembered: *Posted.*
> (T6 · dialogue) *"We are four stones and a painter." Julian counts. "The wall has come to the country."; "The wall has come home, Julian."; "Home. Yes. That is the word."* — remembered: *Home.*
> (T7 · tone) *"Dinner at eight. The campaign eats together." Rose turns for the stairs. "The war office expects punctuality."* — remembered: *Punctuality.*
> (T8 · choice) *They scatter to their rooms, and the house takes them in — the laughed-at, the Frenchman, the soldier, the painter. The garrison is housed. The war has its household.* — remembered: *Housed.*
> *(The lamps are lit, and the Park settles round its people, and Rose stands a moment in the hall with the muster complete: four stones, one wall, and the painter with her sketchbook. The household is gathered. The campaign has its garrison.)*

scenes.synopsis: Monday evening — the first bouquet of the fête week waits in her dressing room; the insult, placed where she must see it. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Monday evening. Her dressing room at the Park — the room she rebuilt first, years ago, the paper she chose herself — and on the dressing table, where her brushes should be, a basket of yellow roses. A dozen. No card. The maid says a boy brought them up with the flower carts, paid, no message.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *A dozen yellow roses, fresh-cut, the thorns stripped. The stripping is the signature by now — even the thorns are too much trouble to leave.* — remembered: *Stripped, as ever.*
> (T2 · examine) *The dressing table. The placement is the message: where she must see them, first thing and last.* — remembered: *Placed to be seen.*
> (T3 · tone) *Dry — "Jealousy, decrease of love. The fourth week running. She has followed me to the Park to say it."* — remembered: *Followed to the Park.*
> (T4 · remembered micro-decision) *The dressing room is hers; the roses are not staying in it. She rings for the maid: the kitchen may have them.* — remembered: *Downstairs.*
> (T5 · stance) *The cook's bower grows — four weeks deep now, carried down from London in the carts. The servants' hall at the Park smells of a florist's.* — remembered: *The bower travels.*
> (T6 · look closer) *The table stands bare again, the brushes back in their places. The room is hers once more.* — remembered: *Hers again.*
> (T7 · choice) *The memorandum book: Monday — yellow roses, the dressing room. Answered in the usual way: downstairs.* — remembered: *The usual way.*
> *(The roses go down the back stairs, and the dressing table stands bare, and the first flower entry of the fête week is written. Cecilia's handwriting, in flowers, has followed her to the Park. The kitchen will enjoy it.)*

scenes.synopsis: Tuesday morning — a second bouquet on the war-office table; Augusta reads the insult dryly. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Tuesday morning. The war office is at work — Augusta with the lists, Letitia with the alphabet — and in the middle of the long table, where the seating plans should be, a basket of yellow roses. A dozen. No card. Somebody brought them in with the morning post and set them down among the papers.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *Yellow roses on the campaign table, shedding petals on the guest list. The insult has found the headquarters.* — remembered: *Headquarters, found.*
> (T2 · examine) *Augusta regards them over her spectacles. "The enemy," she says, "has excellent delivery and deplorable manners."* — remembered: *Deplorable manners.*
> (T3 · tone) *Dry — "Jealousy, decrease of love, Grandmama. On the guest list. She wants the thousand to read it."* — remembered: *For the thousand.*
> (T4 · stance) *"Then the thousand will read it in the kitchen." Augusta does not look up from her lists. "Take them down, child. Petals on the seating plan will not do."* — remembered: *Petals will not do.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *Rose carries the basket down herself, past the maids, to the kitchen — the insult making its usual journey, this time by her own hand.* — remembered: *By her own hand.*
> (T6 · look closer) *The cook receives them like tribute. The bower is now a positive garden. The housemaids have begun a competition for the best stems.* — remembered: *A competition.*
> (T7 · choice) *The memorandum book: Tuesday — yellow roses, the morning room. The headquarters holds. The kitchen blooms.* — remembered: *The kitchen blooms.*
> *(She comes back up to the lists and the plans, and Augusta ticks a name without looking up, and the war office goes on. Two bouquets in two days. The enemy writes in flowers. The headquarters files them downstairs.)*

scenes.synopsis: Tuesday — Élise arrives at the Park with her girls; the whispers have started; the centerpiece is planned. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Tuesday, past eleven. Élise arrives with two girls and a cart of her own — muslins, sketches, the tools of the trade — and she comes up the steps the way she always comes to the Park: like it is hers to dress. But there is something new in the set of her shoulders, and Rose sees it before the greetings are done.)*
> "The whispers have started, darling." Élise does not wait to be asked. "In the shops. 'The modiste's girl dresses the scandal.' They say it lightly. Lightly is how it begins." — Élise
> (T1 · look closer) *The shoulders, the brightness held a fraction too high. Élise is afraid, and doing the brave thing with the fear: bringing it to Rose first.* — remembered: *Brought first.*
> (T2 · tone) *Steady — "Let them whisper, Élise. The town whispered about my painter for a month. The painter is standing."* — remembered: *The painter stands.*
> "The painter had you, darling." Élise's smile is real, underneath. "I have you too. I am counting it." — Élise
> (T3 · stance) *"You have me. Now — the centerpiece. The fête's answer, in flowers. Red roses, and the thorns left on."* — remembered: *Thorns on.*
> (T4 · dialogue) *"Thorns on, darling." Élise's eyes light — the fear going down before the work, the way it always does. "Defiance you can cut yourself on. Oh, I like it. The girls will bleed. They will not mind."* — remembered: *They will not mind.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *They plan it there, on the steps: the great hall, the long table, red roses by the hundred, every thorn left where the stem grew it. The house will answer in flowers.* — remembered: *Planned on the steps.*
> (T6 · examine) *Élise sketches it in the margin of Rose's book — the shape of the defiance, quick and sure. This is the week, Rose sees, that Élise does the finest work of her life so far.* — remembered: *The finest yet.*
> (T7 · tone) *"The town will call it a statement." "The town will call everything a statement, darling. I am past minding what the town calls things."* — remembered: *Past minding.*
> (T8 · choice) *Élise goes in with her girls and her cart, and the atelier of the Park — the old stillroom, given over to her — fills with muslin and purpose. The siege has its dressmaker. The dressmaker is not afraid anymore.* — remembered: *Not afraid.*
> *(The stillroom door stands open, and the chalk is out, and the planning has begun — the centerpiece, the thorns, the answer. The whispers are in the shops. The work is at the Park. Rose knows which one will last the week.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE CENTERPIECE: the form of Rose's answer in flowers — where the thorned red roses stand. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Tuesday night. The counsel of the week is gathered — Augusta's lists, Élise's sketches, the yellow roses in the kitchen, the white rose waiting in the flower room — and the decision sits in the middle of it: the answer. Red roses, thorns on. But the defiance has its shapes, and the shapes have their prices, and the night asks her to choose the shape before the stems arrive.)*
> *(She prices the means: the single defiance — one centerpiece in the great hall, where every guest must pass it; the thorns everywhere — thorned red roses worked through all the fête's flowers, the whole house answering; the quiet thorns — the great hall only, the rest of the fête dressed innocent, the defiance for those who look. Each road answers. Each answers in a different place.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The centerpiece:*
> - **The single defiance** — *One centerpiece, in the great hall: red roses by the hundred, thorns on, where every guest must pass it.* (Consequence: the statement is unmissable — and unmissable is also unmistakable; Cecilia will know exactly where Rose's pride stands.)
> - **The thorns, everywhere** — *Thorned red roses worked through all the fête's flowers — the garlands, the stair, the supper tables — the whole house answering.* (Consequence: the house speaks with one voice — but the work is vast, the week is short, and Élise's girls will bleed for it.)
> - **The quiet thorns** — *Thorns left on the great hall roses only; the rest of the fête dressed innocent. The defiance for those who look closely.* (Consequence: the town's innocent enjoy their flowers undisturbed — but Cecilia may not look closely enough to see it, and an unseen answer is barely an answer.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the unmissable, the everywhere, or the quiet. The stems arrive Thursday. Hers to place.)*
> - (T1) **Choose** — *the single defiance, the thorns everywhere, or the quiet thorns. The shape of the answer is the shape of the defiance.*
> - (T2) **Remembered consequence** — *whichever form it takes, Élise builds it under siege — and the building will be seen. The answer has a cost, and the cost is hers to carry.*
> - (T3) **The road** — *the chosen form, carried to Élise at first light; the centerpiece takes its shape, in the manner Rose chose.*
> *(The book closes on the decision. The answer has its shape now — the defiance, given form. Thursday brings the stems. Tonight the lamp goes out on a week that has learned how to answer.)*
