scenes.synopsis: Wednesday morning — the chosen form of the centerpiece is carried to Élise; the work begins. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Wednesday morning, first light. Rose goes to the stillroom herself, past the hour for calls, with the memorandum book and the decision in it — because some things must be carried by hand, and this is one.)*
> (T1 · stance) *She lays the book open on the worktable: the centerpiece, in its chosen form — the single defiance, the thorns everywhere, or the quiet thorns, whichever she chose. "Read it, Élise. It is yours to build."* — remembered: *Yours to build.*
> (T2 · dialogue) *Élise reads — quickly, twice. "Thorns on." "Thorns on, Élise. Every one the stem grew." "Then the girls will need gloves, darling. And I shall need —" She looks up. "Nothing. I shall need nothing."* — remembered: *Nothing needed.*
> (T3 · look closer) *The fear of yesterday is gone from the shoulders. In its place: the particular brightness Élise gets when the work is worthy of the week.* — remembered: *Worthy of the week.*
> (T4 · tone) *"The town will see the building, Élise. The whispers will have something to whisper about." "Let them, darling. Whispers cannot arrange flowers."* — remembered: *Whispers cannot arrange.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *The red roses are ordered — by the hundred, the best stems, the thorns to be left exactly as cut. The order goes out Wednesday morning.* — remembered: *Ordered by the hundred.*
> (T6 · dialogue) *"You are in the wall too, Élise." "Darling, I am the wall's upholstery. Somebody must make the defiance comfortable to look at."* — remembered: *The upholstery.*
> (T7 · choice) *Rose leaves the book with her — the memorandum, the shape, the thorns. The answer belongs to them both now.* — remembered: *Belongs to both.*
> (T8 · look closer) *On the stair down, she hears the stillroom come alive behind her — the girls, the chalk, the measuring. The week has its music.* — remembered: *Music in the stillroom.*
> *(The stillroom hums, and the order goes out, and the centerpiece stands in its chosen form — planned, in Élise's own hand, on Élise's own terms. The stems come Thursday. The town may whisper. The work is already louder.)*

scenes.synopsis: Wednesday — the fête's flower room; Rose reads the ordered arrangements like dispatches; a white rose where it shouldn't be. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Wednesday. The flower room at the Park — the old dairy, given over for the week — smells of green sap and wet stems and the iron of the buckets. The fête's ordered arrangements stand in rows: the garlands for the great hall, the stair, the supper tables. Rose walks the rows the way Augusta walks the lists: completely.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The great-hall garlands, ordered all red — and worked into the red, single white roses, one to a length. A white rose where it shouldn't be. The wrongness is exact.* — remembered: *Exact wrongness.*
> (T2 · examine) *The stair garlands: yellow rosebuds tucked among the ordered pink, small as a signature. Jealousy, worked into the welcome.* — remembered: *Worked into the welcome.*
> (T3 · tone) *Quiet, to the head gardener — "These were not in the orders." "No, miss." The man's face is miserable. "They came so. In the carts. We thought —" "You thought the carts were the orders. They are not."* — remembered: *Not the orders.*
> (T4 · stance) *She reads every arrangement like a dispatch — the white among the red, the yellow among the pink — and the dispatches all say the same thing: somebody's hand has been in the flowers.* — remembered: *A hand in the flowers.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *The wrong stems come out. Every white rose, every yellow bud, lifted from the ordered garlands and laid aside — quietly, before the town sees.* — remembered: *Lifted quietly.*
> (T6 · look closer) *The laid-aside stems make their own arrangement on the slate: white and yellow, the infiltration's colors. Evidence, in flowers.* — remembered: *Evidence, in flowers.*
> (T7 · choice) *The memorandum book: Wednesday — the flower room, the white rose, the yellow buds. The arrangements read, the wrongness removed. The room gets its guard.* — remembered: *The room guarded.*
> *(She leaves the flower room to its guard — a footman at the door, the gardener with his orders checked twice — and the rows stand correct: red where red was ordered, pink where pink was ordered. The dispatches have been read. The infiltration has been answered with logistics.)*

scenes.synopsis: Wednesday afternoon — Rose walks the dressed grounds: the tents, the kitchens, the lake, the rides; what a fête for a thousand takes. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Wednesday afternoon. Rose walks the grounds with the memorandum book — the tents first, then the kitchens, then the lake and the rides — and the fête for a thousand shows its workings: canvas, timber, chalk, rope.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The great tent: the canvas men are lacing the seams, and the guy-ropes run out to their stakes in long white lines. A thousand guests will dance under this. Today it smells of new rope.* — remembered: *Smell of new rope.*
> (T2 · examine) *The kitchens: the ovens are lit for the trial baking, and the pastry cooks move like a drill. A thousand suppers means the bread alone is a campaign.* — remembered: *Bread, a campaign.*
> (T3 · look closer) *The lake: the boats are out, the lanterns for the water not yet hung. The white posts of the course stand round it like a dotted line.* — remembered: *A dotted line.*
> (T4 · stance) *The rides: the course for the pass, the turf marked, the jumps set low for the grounds' own horses. She walks the whole of it, measuring with her stride.* — remembered: *Measured by stride.*
> (T5 · tone) *Dry, to nobody — "A thousand guests. Three tents, two kitchens, one lake. The arithmetic of pleasure."* — remembered: *Pleasure's arithmetic.*
> (T6 · remembered micro-decision) *The memorandum book fills: the tents, the ovens, the boats, the posts, the jumps. The fête, inventoried.* — remembered: *Inventoried.*
> (T7 · choice) *She stands at the lake's edge with the inventory done and the Park spread round her — dressed, working, hers. The war's set-piece, nearly dressed.* — remembered: *Nearly dressed.*
> *(The canvas men call to each other across the lawn, and the ovens breathe heat into the afternoon, and the lake lies flat under its dotted line of posts. A fête for a thousand takes a village. The village is working. The mistress has walked it.)*

scenes.synopsis: Wednesday — Henry walks Rose through the stables; the equestrian pass announced; the grounds' own horses. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Wednesday, past four. The stables at the Park smell of hay and leather and horse sweat, and Henry walks the lines the way he walks everything: as if it were an inspection and a pleasure at once. The grounds' own horses stand in their boxes — hunters, hacks, the old carriage team — and the grooms touch their caps.)*
> "The pass, Miss Hartwell." Henry stops at a bay mare's box. "The grounds' own horses, ridden round the lake at the fête's opening. A riding week inside the war — the town will come for the flowers and stay for the horses." — Henry
> (T1 · look closer) *The bay mare — sixteen hands, the white sock, the eye of a horse that has seen crowds. The stables are in better order than most regiments.* — remembered: *Better than regiments.*
> (T2 · tone) *"The town will come for the horses first, Henry. The town has its priorities."* — remembered: *Priorities.*
> "The horses first." He nods. "Eight riders, the estate's own — the head groom to lead. The course round the lake, the jumps low. A pass. Dignity, at a canter." — Henry
> (T3 · stance) *"And the riders?" "The grooms, two tenants' sons who ride well, and —" He looks at her. "Whoever else wishes. The mistress, perhaps."* — remembered: *Perhaps the mistress.*
> (T4 · dialogue) *"The mistress rides her own earth, Henry."; "The mistress does. The question is whether she rides it before a thousand guests."; "The question is noted."* — remembered: *Noted.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *She will ride the course herself before the week is out — to check it, the way she checks everything. The pass will be announced tomorrow.* — remembered: *She will ride it.*
> (T6 · examine) *Henry runs a hand down the mare's neck, and the mare leans into it. Soldiers and horses understand each other; it is one of the reliable things.* — remembered: *Reliable things.*
> (T7 · tone) *"You will announce it at dinner, Henry. The pass. The town loves a soldier with news." "The town loves a soldier, Miss Hartwell. The news is incidental."* — remembered: *Incidental news.*
> (T8 · choice) *They walk the lines together, and the stables settle round them — the hay, the leather, the sweat, the order. The pass has its stager. The horses are ready.* — remembered: *Ready.*
> *(The lamps are lit in the stable yard, and the horses blow soft in their boxes, and the pass is a plan with a stager and a course. Eight riders, the lake, the jumps low. Dignity, at a canter. The fête will open with horses.)*

scenes.synopsis: Wednesday evening — Élise lays out three habits for the course ride; Rose chooses the face of the rider. (Turns: 6)
scenes.prose:
> *(Wednesday evening, the stillroom. Between the centerpiece sketches, Élise has been thinking about the ride — Rose can see the thinking in the three habits on the forms, each one cut for the saddle. "For the course," Élise says. "You must look like the Park's mistress before you look like anything else." She lays out the three the way a general lays out maps.)*
> - (T1) **The Chatelaine** — *deep green habit, the Park's own color; the oak in gold at the collar; colorway green, gold, cream; the gold stock pin; her grandmother's pearls under the collar; the beaver hat, veiled.* — remembered: *She considers the Chatelaine.*
> - (T2) **The Huntress** — *dark brown habit, severe; the rider, stated; the oak in bronze at the cuff; colorway brown, bronze, cream; the bronze stock pin; pearl drop earrings; the beaver hat, unveiled.* — remembered: *She considers the Huntress.*
> - (T3) **The Sovereign** — *black habit, absolute; the mistress, declared; the oak in jet at the collar, dark on dark; colorway black, jet, pearl; the jet stock pin; a single pearl pin; the beaver hat, veiled.* — remembered: *She considers the Sovereign.*
> - (T4) **Choose** — *the considering done; the habit for the course, chosen — the rider's face for the thousand.* — remembered: *She has chosen.*
> - (T5) **The fitting's note** — *Élise takes the measurements herself and says, "Sit tall, Rose. The course is yours. The habit only says so."* — remembered: *Sit tall.*
> - (T6) **Remembered micro-decision** — *The course ride is Thursday morning, early, before the town wakes. The habit will be ready.* — remembered: *Ready by Thursday.*
> *(The muslin is pinned, the habit chosen, and Élise steps back with chalk on her fingers and the particular brightness of a woman dressing two wars at once. The course is hers. The habit will say so. Thursday morning, early — the rider rides out.)*

scenes.synopsis: Thursday morning, early — Rose rides out to check the course; the rider she is. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Thursday, half past six. The Park is empty but for the birds and the stable yard, and Rose rides out in the chosen habit — the bay mare with the white sock under her, the course round the lake ahead. The morning is cold, and the mare is fresh, and the world is reduced to the good things: the saddle, the stride, the ground.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The mare moves out sweetly, the white sock flashing. Sixteen hands of estate-bred sense, and Rose feels the weeks fall off her shoulders with every stride.* — remembered: *Shoulders lighten.*
> (T2 · examine) *The course: the white posts, the turf, the jumps set low. She takes them in order — the lake on her left, the tents white in the distance — and the mare never hesitates.* — remembered: *Never hesitates.*
> (T3 · stance) *She rides the full circuit twice — once to see it, once to know it. The rider she is: the girl who learned on this turf, the woman who rebuilt the ground under it.* — remembered: *Twice round.*
> (T4 · tone) *To the mare, low — "Good girl. The thousand will love you. Try not to let it go to your head."* — remembered: *No swelled head.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *The turf is good, the jumps are fair, the lake bend wants the posts moved two yards out — she notes it for Henry. The course is hers now.* — remembered: *Posts moved out.*
> (T6 · look closer) *The sun comes up over the tents, and the canvas goes gold, and the Park lies round her — dressed, working, waiting. Her earth, under hoof.* — remembered: *Under hoof.*
> (T7 · choice) *She walks the mare home cool, and the stable yard wakes round them, and the memorandum book gets the line: Thursday — the course, ridden, known. The pass will do.* — remembered: *The pass will do.*
> *(The mare is rubbed down, and the habit is brushed, and Rose walks back to the house with the morning in her blood. The town will see the rider on Sunday. The rider has seen the course first. That is the order of things.)*

scenes.synopsis: Thursday — Laurent walks the dressed grounds with Rose; his eye, his beat at the Park. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Thursday, past eleven. Laurent walks the grounds with Rose — the tents, the lake, the flower carts — and he does it the way he does everything at the Park: as if he were deciding whether to approve, and approving in spite of himself.)*
> "Chérie." He stops at the lake's edge. "A thousand guests. Tents like sails. Horses." He spreads his hands. "It is magnificent. It is also, if you will forgive the observation, completely mad." — Laurent
> (T1 · tone) *Dry — "Mad, Laurent? The French do not do mad?"* — remembered: *She calls him mad.*
> "The French do mad beautifully, chérie. The English do it —" He looks at the guy-ropes. "With rope. It is charming. I am charmed." — Laurent
> (T2 · look closer) *The polish is all there — the ease, the hands — but underneath it the man the assembly made: the one who set down his ruin in public and kept walking.* — remembered: *Underneath, the man.*
> (T3 · stance) *"The pass." He nods at the white posts. "You will ride it, chérie? Before the thousand?"* — remembered: *He asks it.*
> (T4 · dialogue) *"I rode it this morning, Laurent. Twice. The mare and I have an understanding."; "Twice, before breakfast. The English —"; "The English ride, Laurent."* — remembered: *The English ride.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *He will take the French guests — the de Valcourt cousins, the attachés — and keep them charmed and out of the flower room. Laurent's station, set.* — remembered: *The French are his to charm.*
> (T6 · tone) *"And Cecilia, chérie?" The polish thins. "She will come to this. You know she will."* — remembered: *She will come.*
> (T7 · dialogue) *"Let her come, Laurent. The ground is mine. The flowers are mine. The thorns are mine."; "The thorns, chérie?"; "You will see them Sunday."* — remembered: *Sunday.*
> (T8 · choice) *He kisses her hand, and the gesture has the unpracticed feeling underneath — the weeks have taught him the difference, and he no longer hides it.* — remembered: *No longer hidden.*
> *(They walk back past the tents, and the canvas men touch their caps, and Laurent surveys the campaign with a Frenchman's eye and finds it — against his better judgment — magnificent. The ground has its Frenchman. The Frenchman has his station.)*

scenes.synopsis: the fête week's ritual — dress for war on her own ground; direction + twenty 5-coin pins, story morsels between, reveal coda. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "Hartwell Park, Saturday. Miss Hartwell will walk her own grounds before a thousand guests, in the full view of the ton — and of her enemy. The dress code of the fête week: armor — the armor of the mistress of the ground. The gown must hold a park, a campaign, and a war. **Editorial criterion: the ground, held.**"
>
> **A. The Standard** — crimson silk, Hartwell crimson; the mistress's color, declared. Motif: the Hartwell oak in gold thread at the shoulder — the house, stated. Thread: **gold** (the ground, held) / **copper** (the warmth of the house) / **crimson silk** (the house, matched). Colorway: crimson + gold + cream. Accessories: the gold oak brooch; her grandmother's pearls; red rosebuds at the wrist, the thorns left on.
> **B. The Chatelaine** — deep green silk, the Park's own color; the ground, worn. Motif: the oak worked in gold at the hem — the house, restrained. Thread: **gold** (the ground, held) / **bronze** (the autumn, acknowledged) / **green silk** (the Park, matched). Colorway: green + gold + cream. Accessories: the pearl drop earrings; her grandmother's pearls; red rosebuds at the wrist, the thorns left on.
> **C. The Commander** — black silk, severe; the campaign, stated. Motif: the oak in jet at the shoulder, dark on dark — stitched to be watched. Thread: **jet** (the ground, held) / **black silk** (the campaign, matched) / **grey whitework** (the ground, lit). Colorway: black + jet + pearl. Accessories: the jet oak brooch; a single pearl pin; red rosebuds at the wrist, the thorns left on.
>
> *(The dressing room at the Park, the hour of the fête week: armor of the ground for the campaign — the stated, the worn, the hers. She dresses the way the week has dressed her: to hold her own earth before a thousand guests.)*
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *She commits: the Standard, the Chatelaine, or the Commander — the thesis of the fête week, remembered. The hair, composed. The accessories, exact. The mirror, to be consulted briefly. **Direction.** Hartwell Park, Saturday — the grounds, the guests, the enemy watching. Dress to hold her own earth. **Editorial criterion.** The ground, held — every choice must show the mistress, not the shadow of the armor.*
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the fête week. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins — 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins; no Crown SKUs; jewels from owned pieces only, never a ritual step.)*
> **Pin 1 (T2 · micro-decision) — Gown, chosen:** the face of the week — the crimson stated, the green worn, or the black severe — whichever the ground chose, the armor worn. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 (T3 · micro-decision) — Fit, exact:** composed — no rustle for the hush of the great hall, no train for the judgment of the thousand. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 (T4 · micro-decision) — Sleeves, long:** for the week — composed, unhurried, giving the watchers nothing. *5 coins.*
> *(The pins accumulate — the line of the gown set, the sleeves of the week — and the dressing room holds its morning light the way the stillroom holds its chalk: patiently. Élise pins the hem herself and says, "The ground, held, Rose. They must see the mistress. That is the whole of it.")*
> **Pin 4 (T5 · micro-decision) — Neckline, open:** the command — the throat uncovered, the face unshadowed; the thousand read openness first. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — Hair, coiled:** braided — composed and kept; no ornament. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — Ribbon, at the throat:** the punctuation of the direction — gold, bronze, or black — the ground, tied. *5 coins.*
> *(The ribbon tied — the knot of the ground — and the morning leans in, the hour of the campaign waiting. Through the window, the tents stand white on the lawn, and the lake lies flat. The Park is dressed. She will match it.)*
> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — Gloves, kid, close:** for the week — the hands of the mistress, gloved for the receiving; the town can read the closeness. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T9 · micro-decision) — Slippers, quiet:** of the stairs — the stair of the great hall, unheard. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — Fan, carried:** the companion of the reticule — the punctuation of the receiving, unopened. *5 coins.*
> *(Quiet slippers, the weight of the fan — the receiving asks for quiet, and she gives it.)*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — Brooch, the oak:** of the direction — gold or jet — the small heraldry, pinned at the shoulder. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — Scent, none:** for the week — no perfume for the air of the flower room; the town smells the roses, not the lady. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — Posture, straight:** of the mistress — held and offered; the answer of the spine to the thousand. *5 coins.*
> *(The spine straightens — offered and held — and the mirror is consulted briefly from the corner of her eye. Red rosebuds at the wrist, the thorns left on, pinned small where she will feel them all week.)*
> **Pin 13 (T14 · micro-decision) — Gaze, level:** of the week — met eye to eye, the thousand's. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T15 · micro-decision) — Voice, measured:** of the campaign — the guests count the words; measured is command. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T16 · micro-decision) — Hands, still:** of the receiving — held, composed; the bareness shown at the wrist, thorns and all. *5 coins.*
> *(Level gaze, measured voice, still hands — the instruments of the mistress, tuned for the light of the great hall.)*
> **Pin 16 (T17 · micro-decision) — Step, measured:** of the stairs — of Saturday, descended. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T18 · micro-decision) — Smile, worn:** of the week — the open, the unhidden; the whole meaning of the ground, held. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T19 · micro-decision) — Pearls, her grandmother's:** at the throat — continuity, worn; Hartwell continuity, stated. *5 coins.*
> *(The pearls at the throat — the continuity, stated — and the morning light of the dressing room does its final work. In the corner of the stillroom, under its sheet, the shape of the fête gown waits — the most magnificent of the series, Élise says, and will say no more. Sunday's gown. This week's is armor.)*
> **Pin 19 (T20 · micro-decision) — Reticule, weighted:** of the week — the memorandum book within, the pencil, the guest list, the course map; and folded small beside them, the thorn of a red rose — the answer, carried. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T21 · micro-decision) — The door, faced:** the last pin is not a pin — it is the turning toward the stairs, the face of the week set, the ground held whole. *5 coins.*
> *(The reveal: the stairs descended, the door of the hall opened, the Park waiting — the fête week, dressed. The gown is the answer of the week before the thousand arrive: the ground, held. The coda of the ritual is not a mirror. It is the south lawn ahead — the tents, the lake, the thousand to come — and the stand, worn like the gown: armor, the ground held, hers.)*

ritual.occasionBrief: the fête week at Hartwell Park; the preparations; the war, moved to her own ground.

scenes.synopsis: Thursday afternoon — Julian's beat at the Park; the town's talk, his station. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Thursday afternoon. Julian walks the tent lines with Rose, his unread book under his arm, and he does it with the particular pleasure of a man who has been given a station and intends to deserve it.)*
> "The town's talk is my department, Rose. I have been practicing." He straightens. "I told three matrons at the posting inn that the fête will be the event of the decade. One of them believed me. The other two are considering it." — Julian
> (T1 · tone) *Warm — "Considering it, Julian. You are wasted on the town. The town does not deserve you."* — remembered: *Wasted on the town.*
> "The town is getting me anyway." He grins — the old Julian, entire. "I am to ride in the pass, Rose. Henry has given me the grey. I have been practicing being dignified at a canter. It is harder than it looks." — Julian
> (T2 · look closer) *The grin is the old Julian. The practicing is the new one. They sit side by side in him now without quarreling.* — remembered: *Old and new agree.*
> (T3 · stance) *"You will be dignified, Julian. The grey would not stand for otherwise."* — remembered: *The grey insists.*
> "The grey is a snob." He sobers, the way he does now — quickly, without performance. "Rose. The mended gloves." He touches the cuff. "The town laughed at them once. On Sunday the town will watch me ride past in them. I have been thinking about that." — Julian
> (T4 · dialogue) *"And?"; "And I find I do not mind. The gloves are mine. The laugh was theirs. The ride will be mine too."; "Then ride it, Julian."* — remembered: *The ride is his.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *She will watch him pass from the stands — or the saddle, whichever she chose — and the town will see the laughed-at riding the Park's own grey. The wall rides.* — remembered: *The wall rides.*
> (T6 · tone) *"Cecilia will be watching, you know." "Let her watch. I was laughed at in print, Rose. Print is weather. The grey is real."* — remembered: *The grey is real.*
> (T7 · social maneuver) *"Then Sunday. The pass. Dignity, at a canter." "Dignity." He bows. "I shall be so dignified the matrons will weep."* — remembered: *Weeping matrons.*
> (T8 · choice) *He goes off to practice — the dignified canter, the grey, the gloves — and the tent lines settle behind him. The young lord has his station. The station suits him.* — remembered: *Suited.*
> *(The canvas flaps in the afternoon wind, and Julian goes to his practicing with his book unread and his dignity rehearsed, and Rose stands with the certainty of the week: the laughed-at is riding in the pass, in his mended gloves, before a thousand guests. The town laughed once. The town will watch now.)*

scenes.synopsis: Thursday — Augusta walks Rose through the fête kitchens; the logistics of a thousand suppers. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Thursday, past five. The fête kitchens behind the east wing breathe heat into the evening — the ovens lit, the trial baking done, the pastry cooks at their drill. Augusta walks the lines with Rose, tasting, nodding, finding fault the way other women find conversation.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The bread for a thousand: the loaves in rows, the ovens like small furnaces. Augusta breaks a loaf, tastes, nods once. The nod is the whole of the review.* — remembered: *One nod.*
> (T2 · examine) *The chalk sums on the boards — the numbers for Sunday, the courses, the wines. Somebody's arithmetic, in chalk, where the cooks can see it.* — remembered: *Chalk arithmetic.*
> (T3 · tone) *Augusta, to the head cook — "The soup wants salt. The town will forgive many things, but it will not forgive unsalted soup."* — remembered: *Salt the soup.*
> (T4 · stance) *"The numbers, Grandmama?" "The kitchens have them. Thursday, as promised. The campaign eats on schedule."* — remembered: *On schedule.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *Rose walks the whole of it — the ovens, the larders, the wine going down to the cellars by the dozen. The logistics of pleasure, inspected.* — remembered: *Inspected.*
> (T6 · dialogue) *"You ran campaigns, Grandmama."; "I ran households, child. The difference is smaller than the town thinks."; "The town thinks a great deal."* — remembered: *Smaller than thought.*
> (T7 · choice) *They come out into the evening with the smell of bread in their clothes, and Augusta ticks the kitchens off her list — done, in chalk. The campaign eats.* — remembered: *The campaign eats.*
> *(The ovens breathe on behind them, and the pastry cooks go back to their drill, and the kitchens stand ready: a thousand suppers, on schedule, salted. Augusta has inspected. The town will be fed.)*

scenes.synopsis: Thursday evening — the lake at dusk; the rides, the boats, the water; the Park before the thousand. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Thursday evening. Rose walks down to the lake alone, past the white posts of the course, and the water lies flat under the dusk — the boats pulled up, the lanterns for the water not yet hung, the tents white behind her on the lawn.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *The lake at dusk: the far bank dark, the water holding the last light. She has swum here, ridden round it, rebuilt the banks stone by stone.* — remembered: *Stone by stone.*
> (T2 · examine) *The white posts of the course stand round the water like a dotted line — the pass's route, waiting for Sunday. The jumps sit low and fair.* — remembered: *Low and fair.*
> (T3 · tone) *Quiet, to the water — "You have seen fêtes before. You will see this one."* — remembered: *Seen before.*
> (T4 · stance) *She stands a while with the dusk coming on — the mistress of the ground, alone with the ground, before the thousand take it for a day.* — remembered: *Alone with it.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *The lanterns for the water go up Saturday — she notes it for the memorandum. The lake will wear lights on Sunday.* — remembered: *Lights Saturday.*
> (T6 · look closer) *A moorhen crosses the flat water, unhurried, unimpressed by fêtes. Somebody at the Park is not thinking about Sunday.* — remembered: *One unmoved bird.*
> (T7 · choice) *She turns back up the lawn with the dusk behind her — the lake, the posts, the tents, the house with its lamps lit. The Park, before the thousand.* — remembered: *Before the thousand.*
> *(The water keeps the last light a little longer, and the moorhen crosses and recrosses, and the Park settles into its dusk shape: dressed, waiting, hers. Sunday brings the thousand. Tonight the lake is hers alone.)*

scenes.synopsis: Friday morning — Letitia and the invitations; the weight of a thousand names, and the funny of it. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Friday morning. The war office is knee-deep in acceptances — the morning post has brought them by the sack — and Letitia sits in the middle of it with a pencil behind her ear and the air of a woman who has survived something.)*
> "The thousand, darling." Letitia waves a stack. "Eight hundred and forty-two acceptances. Ninety-one regrets. Sixty-seven who have not answered, who are, I have decided, dead." — Letitia
> (T1 · tone) *Dry — "Dead, Aunt? Sixty-seven?"* — remembered: *Sixty-seven dead.*
> "Dead to me, darling. Which is worse. The dead at least do not require chairs." — Letitia
> (T2 · look closer) *The stacks, the sacks, the pencil behind the ear. Letitia has written a thousand names and kept her humor. It is the greater achievement.* — remembered: *Humor kept.*
> (T3 · dialogue) *"The weight of them, Aunt." Rose lifts a stack. "A thousand invitations. The paper alone —"; "Weighed a stone, darling. I weighed it. For science."; "For science."* — remembered: *A stone of paper.*
> (T4 · stance) *"And the sixty-seven?" "Augusta is writing to them. Personally. The sixty-seven will answer or perish."* — remembered: *Answer or perish.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *Letitia will keep the lists of who came — "for the memoirs, darling" — and Rose does not ask what memoirs.* — remembered: *For the memoirs.*
> (T6 · tone) *"You have done the thousand, Aunt." "I have done the thousand, darling. I am now going to lie down in a dark room and be a person again."* — remembered: *A person again.*
> (T7 · choice) *She goes, and the war office settles — eight hundred and forty-two acceptances, the chairs counted, the campaign fed. The thousand are coming.* — remembered: *They are coming.*
> *(The sacks are emptied, and the stacks are sorted, and Letitia goes to her dark room with the pencil still behind her ear. Eight hundred and forty-two. The Park will hold them. The mistress will receive them.)*

scenes.synopsis: Friday — yellow roses in the fête's own flower room; the insult, worked into the week's flowers. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Friday. The flower room at the Park — the guard at the door, the gardener with his orders checked twice — and on the slate where the laid-aside stems were, a fresh basket. Yellow roses. A dozen. No card. Somebody set them among the week's flowers like a signature.)*
> (T1 · look closer) *Yellow roses in the flower room itself — the room where the fête's flowers are dressed. The insult has come to the source.* — remembered: *To the source.*
> (T2 · examine) *No card, no ribbon. The basket sits among the buckets like it belongs. It does not belong.* — remembered: *Does not belong.*
> (T3 · tone) *Dry — "Jealousy, decrease of love. In the flower room. She is nothing if not thorough."* — remembered: *Thorough.*
> (T4 · stance) *She reads the room again — every garland, every bucket — the way she read it Wednesday. The ordered flowers stand correct. The basket stands incorrect.* — remembered: *Correct and incorrect.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *The basket goes downstairs with the others — the kitchen bower is now beyond competition, beyond measure. The cook has stopped commenting.* — remembered: *Beyond measure.*
> (T6 · look closer) *The guard is questioned — he saw no one, the door was watched, the basket was simply there. Somebody's hand is quicker than a footman.* — remembered: *Quicker than a footman.*
> (T7 · choice) *The memorandum book: Friday — yellow roses, the flower room. The infiltration's colors, filed. The room keeps its guard.* — remembered: *Guard kept.*
> *(The basket goes down the back stairs, and the flower room stands correct behind its guard, and the week's flowers are read and re-read. Three bouquets in the house, one in the flower room. The enemy writes in flowers. The mistress reads them all.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE PASS: Rose's place in the equestrian pass — whether she rides before the thousand. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Friday night. The counsel of the week is gathered — Henry's course, the bay mare, Julian on the grey, the habit chosen and waiting — and the decision sits in the middle of it: the ride. The pass opens the fête. The mistress may lead it, join it, or watch it. Each road rides. Each rides in a different place.)*
> *(She prices the means: ride at the head — the mistress leading the pass herself, on the grounds' own horses, before the thousand; ride the opening turn — the first circuit in the saddle, then the stands with Augusta, the gesture made and the risk banked; watch from the stands — the mistress receiving, the riders riding, no risk to her person. Each road is hers. Each costs differently.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — The pass:*
> - **Ride at the head** — *Rose leads the pass herself — the bay mare, the full course, the thousand watching the mistress ride her own earth.* (Consequence: the town sees the rider she is — and Cecilia sees exactly where to aim; a fall, a spooked horse, a thousand witnesses.)
> - **Ride the opening turn** — *She rides the first circuit, then takes the stands with Augusta; the gesture made, the risk banked.* (Consequence: the town gets its picture and the Park keeps its mistress — but half a ride is half a statement, and the town knows halves.)
> - **Watch from the stands** — *She declines the saddle and watches with the garrison; the mistress receives, the riders ride.* (Consequence: no risk to her person — and the one thing Cecilia cannot take from the fête is the one thing Rose did not give it: herself, riding.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the head, the turn, or the stands. The pass rides Sunday. Hers to place.)*
> - (T1) **Choose** — *ride at the head, ride the opening turn, or watch from the stands. The shape of the ride is the shape of the statement.*
> - (T2) **Remembered consequence** — *whichever road, the course is hers — she rode it Thursday, twice, and knows every post. The riding is the truth; the placing is the choice.*
> - (T3) **The road** — *the chosen road, carried to Henry at first light; the pass takes its order, in the manner Rose chose.*
> *(The book closes on the decision. The ride has its shape now — the statement, given form. Sunday brings the thousand. Tonight the lamp goes out on a mistress who knows her course.)*

scenes.synopsis: Saturday morning — the chosen place in the pass is carried to Henry; the order of the ride is set. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Saturday morning, first light. Rose goes to the stables herself, past the hour for calls, with the memorandum book and the decision in it — because some things must be carried by hand, and this is one.)*
> (T1 · stance) *She lays the book open on the tack-room table: the pass, in its chosen order — the head, the opening turn, or the stands, whichever she chose. "Read it, Henry. It is yours to stage."* — remembered: *Yours to stage.*
> (T2 · dialogue) *Henry reads — once, exactly. "The order is set." "The order is set, Henry. Eight riders, the lake, the jumps low." "Dignity, at a canter."* — remembered: *Dignity, at a canter.*
> (T3 · look closer) *The tack room smells of leather and saddle soap. The bridles hang in their rows, each one checked. Henry stages a pass the way he stages everything: completely.* — remembered: *Completely.*
> (T4 · tone) *"Julian rides the grey." "Julian rides the grey, Miss Hartwell. He has been practicing dignity. The grey approves."* — remembered: *The grey approves.*
> (T5 · remembered micro-decision) *The order goes out Saturday morning — the riders, the places, the course. The head groom takes it like a commission.* — remembered: *Like a commission.*
> (T6 · dialogue) *"And the mare?" "The bay is ready, Miss Hartwell. Whatever the order asks of her."; "The order asks a great deal."; "She will give it."* — remembered: *She will give it.*
> (T7 · choice) *Rose leaves the book with him — the memorandum, the order, the pass. The ride belongs to them both now.* — remembered: *Belongs to both.*
> (T8 · look closer) *On the yard out, she hears the stables come alive behind her — the horses, the grooms, the tack. The week has its music.* — remembered: *Music in the stables.*
> *(The stable yard hums, and the order goes out, and the pass stands in its chosen order — planned, in Henry's own hand, on Henry's own terms. The riders know their places. Sunday brings the thousand. The horses are ready.)*

scenes.synopsis: Saturday — Augusta runs the campaign's last full day; absolute, and funny about it. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(Saturday. The war office is at full stretch — the lists closing, the chairs counted, the kitchens on schedule — and Augusta sits at the head of it like a monarch who has abolished opposition. Letitia has stopped pacing. Nobody paces when Augusta is absolute.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE LIST: the guest list closes; Rose chooses how the fête holds its ground against the infiltration. (Turns: 3 — the decision)

> *(Saturday night. The counsel of the week is gathered — Augusta's closed lists, the flower room's guard, the wrong stems filed, the yellow roses in the kitchen — and the decision sits in the middle of it: the ground. > *(She prices the means: hold the list open — every invitation stands, the gates open, the war fought in the open on her ground; cut the doubtful — the doubtful names quietly withdrawn, the gates narrowed, a smaller fête and a safer one; set the watch — the list stands, and the household becomes eyes, every room watched, the fête guarded like a campaign. Each road holds. Each holds differently.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — The list:*
> - **Hold the list open** — *Every invitation stands; the gates open; let them come and be watched. The war fought in the open, on her ground.* (Consequence: the infiltrators walk in with the guests — and the watching must never blink, all day, in every room.)

> - **Set the watch** — *The list stands, and the household becomes eyes: every room with a watcher, every toast heard, the fête guarded like a campaign.* (Consequence: nothing will happen unseen — but a watched fête is a nervous one, and the guests will feel the watching.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the open, the cut, or the watch. The list closes tonight. Hers to place.)*

> - (T2) **Remembered consequence** — *whichever road, the flowers proved the infiltration — and the proving means the holding must be real. The ground is held, or it is not.*
> - (T3) **The road** — *the chosen road, walked Saturday night; the list closes in the manner Rose chose.*
> *(The book closes on the decision. The ground has its holding now — the mistress, given form. Tomorrow the thousand come. Tonight the lamp goes out on a week that has learned how to hold.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE RECEIVING: how Rose receives the thousand at the fête's opening. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday, half past ten. The counsel of the morning is gathered — Augusta's lists, Letitia's headquarters, the garrison's stations — and the decision sits in the middle of it: the receiving. The thousand come at noon. The mistress may stand to receive them, walk among them, or let the garrison receive while she arrives as the spectacle. Each road receives. Each receives differently.)*
> *(She prices the means: the great line — at the steps with Augusta at her shoulder, every guest presented, the formality absolute; the walk — no line, the mistress moving among the guests on her own grounds, the receiving done walking; the garrison receives — the four and the household receive in shifts, and she arrives at the pass as the day's spectacle. Each road is hers. Each costs differently.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The receiving:*
> - **The great line** — *She receives at the steps with Augusta at her shoulder — every guest presented, the Dowager's weight where the thousand can see it.* (Consequence: the town sees the establishment receive — and Cecilia, arriving, must walk the line and be presented like any guest.)
> - **The walk** — *No line; she moves among the guests on the grounds — the mistress walking her own earth, the receiving done in motion.* (Consequence: the thousand meet her on her ground — but she cannot be everywhere, and the rooms she is not in will talk.)
> - **The garrison receives** — *The four and the household receive in shifts; she arrives at the pass as the spectacle — the gown, the noon light, the thousand watching.* (Consequence: the arrival is magnificent — and the receiving is delegated, and the town will note whose hands did it.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the line, the walk, or the garrison. The thousand come at noon. Hers to place.)*
> - (T1) **Choose** — *the great line, the walk, or the garrison receives. The shape of the receiving is the shape of the mistress.*
> - (T2) **Remembered consequence** — *whichever road, the thousand come — and the coming is the thing; the manner is the means. The receiving is hers.*
> - (T3) **The road** — *the chosen road, carried to Augusta and Letitia before eleven; the receiving takes its order, in the manner Rose chose.*
> *(The book closes on the decision. The receiving has its shape now — the mistress, given form. Eleven brings the gown. Noon brings the thousand.)*

scenes.synopsis: the fête's ritual — the most magnificent gown of the series; direction + twenty 5-coin pins, story morsels between, reveal coda. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "Hartwell Park, Sunday noon. Miss Hartwell will open her fête before a thousand guests — and before her enemy — in the most magnificent gown of the series: Hartwell colors, ten seasons of taste, worn on her own ground while Cecilia watches. Beauty as a weapon of war: let them look, and let the looking cost them. **Editorial criterion: let them look — and let the looking cost them.**"
>
> **A. The Hartwell Crimson** — crimson silk, the house's color, declared. Motif: the Hartwell oak worked in gold thread across the full skirt — ten seasons in the stitching, the house stated. Thread: **gold** (the ten seasons) / **copper** (the warmth of the house) / **crimson silk** (the house, matched). Colorway: crimson + gold + cream. Accessories: the great gold oak brooch; her grandmother's pearls; a thorned red rose at the shoulder.
> **B. The Sovereign Green** — deep green silk, the Park's own color, worn. Motif: oak leaves in gold at the hem, the lake worked in silver thread at the waist — the ground, worn. Thread: **gold** (the ground, held) / **silver** (the lake, lit) / **green silk** (the Park, matched). Colorway: green + gold + pearl. Accessories: the pearl drop earrings; her grandmother's pearls; the gold oak comb; a thorned red rose at the wrist.
> **C. The Ten-Season Cloth** — ivory silk, the past worn as proof. Motif: ten oak sprigs in gold and crimson thread, one for each season, worked up the skirt — the triumphs, counted. Thread: **gold** (the seasons) / **crimson silk** (the house) / **ivory** (the proof). Colorway: ivory + crimson + gold. Accessories: her grandmother's pearls, doubled; the gold oak brooch; a thorned red rose at the throat.
>
> *(The stillroom at the Park, the dressing hour: the most magnificent of the series, under its sheet no longer — the stated, the worn, the proof. She dresses the way the series has dressed her: ten seasons, one gown.)*
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *She commits: the Hartwell Crimson, the Sovereign Green, or the Ten-Season Cloth — the thesis of the fête, remembered. The hair, composed. The accessories, exact. The mirror, to be consulted briefly. **Direction.** Hartwell Park, Sunday noon — the thousand, the pass, the enemy watching. Dress to be looked at, and to make the looking cost. **Editorial criterion.** Let them look — every choice must show the mistress at her most magnificent, never the shadow of the armor.*
> *(System: commit to a direction — remembered for the fête. Then the pins begin. Each pin costs 5 coins — 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins; no Crown SKUs; jewels from owned pieces only, never a ritual step.)*
> **Pin 1 (T2 · micro-decision) — Gown, chosen:** the face of the fête — the crimson declared, the green worn, or the ivory proved — whichever the series chose, the magnificence worn. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 2 (T3 · micro-decision) — Fit, exact:** cut close — the silk to show the figure the town will talk about, the seaming invisible. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 3 (T4 · micro-decision) — Sleeves, short:** for the noon light — the arms bare to the elbow, the bracelets given their hour. *5 coins.*
> *(The pins accumulate — the line of the gown set, the sleeves of the noon — and the stillroom holds its morning light the way the great hall holds its roses: patiently. Élise lifts the sheet, and the gown stands revealed, and Rose looks at it for a long moment without speaking.)*
> **Pin 4 (T5 · micro-decision) — Neckline, low:** the command — the throat and shoulders given to the light; the thousand read beauty first. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 5 (T6 · micro-decision) — Hair, dressed high:** piled and pinned — the neck lengthened, the pearls given their stage. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 6 (T7 · micro-decision) — Ribbon, none:** no ribbon for the fête — the gown needs no punctuation; the magnificence speaks. *5 coins.*
> *(No ribbon — the knot undone, the hour of the spectacle waiting. Through the stillroom window, the drive fills with carriages, and the lake lies flat. The Park is dressed. She will outdress it.)*
> **Pin 7 (T8 · micro-decision) — Gloves, elbow, close:** for the receiving — the arms gloved to the elbow, the kid pale against the silk. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 8 (T9 · micro-decision) — Slippers, silk:** of the direction — dyed to the gown, the heel high, the stair descended slowly. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 9 (T10 · micro-decision) — Fan, painted:** the companion of the weapon — the Hartwell oak on ivory sticks, opened for the thousand. *5 coins.*
> *(The fan painted — the oak on ivory — and the receiving asks for spectacle, and she gives it.)*
> **Pin 10 (T11 · micro-decision) — Brooch, the oak:** of the direction — the great gold brooch, the state piece — pinned where the thousand will see it first. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 11 (T12 · micro-decision) — Scent, orange-flower:** for the noon — the flower water, light; the town smells the roses, and beneath them, her. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 12 (T13 · micro-decision) — Posture, held:** of the mistress — the spine the gown was cut for; the answer of the figure to the thousand. *5 coins.*
> *(The spine held — the gown's own line — and Élise steps back with chalk on her fingers. "Ten seasons, Rose," she says. "Every one of them in the stitching. Let them look.")*
> **Pin 13 (T14 · micro-decision) — Gaze, direct:** of the fête — met eye to eye, the thousand's; the beauty given straight. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 14 (T15 · micro-decision) — Voice, low:** of the spectacle — the guests lean in to hear; the leaning is the point. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 15 (T16 · micro-decision) — Hands, shown:** of the noon — ungloved at the wrist where the thorned rose is pinned, the bareness deliberate. *5 coins.*
> *(Direct gaze, low voice, shown hands — the instruments of the spectacle, tuned for the noon light of the great hall.)*
> **Pin 16 (T17 · micro-decision) — Step, slow:** of the stairs — of noon, descended; the magnificence takes its time. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 17 (T18 · micro-decision) — Smile, given:** of the fête — the open, the unhidden; the whole meaning of the looking, priced. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 18 (T19 · micro-decision) — Pearls, her grandmother's:** at the throat — continuity, worn; ten seasons' continuity, stated. *5 coins.*
> *(The pearls at the throat — the continuity, stated — and the stillroom light does its final work. The thorned red rose is pinned — at the shoulder, the wrist, or the throat, where the direction placed it — the answer, worn.)*
> **Pin 19 (T20 · micro-decision) — Reticule, silk:** of the gown — dyed to match, the memorandum book left behind; today she carries nothing but the looking. *5 coins.*
> **Pin 20 (T21 · micro-decision) — The door, faced:** the last pin is not a pin — it is the turning toward the stairs, the face of the fête set, the magnificence whole. *5 coins.*
> *(The reveal: the stairs descended at noon, the great hall full, the thousand turning — the most magnificent of the series, worn on her own ground while her enemy watches. The coda of the ritual is not a mirror. It is the looking, and the cost of it: they look, and it costs them.)*

> *(Wednesday evening, past six. The dressing room — the gown waiting below, the river hour coming — and the decision sits in the middle of it: the lamps. The gardens open at dusk, and the thousand lamps are lit seemingly at once, and the party must meet the night in some manner. Each road meets it. Each meets it differently.)*
> *(She prices the means: the bright paths — walk the bright walks from the first lamp, the garrison visible, the dark walks' game refused outright; the supper box — take Augusta's box early and hold it as headquarters, the ham, the punch, the station; the lighting — arrive at the lamps' lighting itself, the crowd's roar, the spectacle of the entrance. Each road is hers. Each costs differently.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The lamps:*
> - **The bright paths** — *She walks the bright walks from the first lamp — the garrison visible, the refusal of the dark walks' game stated in the walking.* (Consequence: the town sees the warrior in the light from the first — and the dark walks will talk unwitnessed, and she will not hear it.)
> - **The supper box** — *She takes Augusta's box early and holds it as headquarters — the ham, the arrack punch, the station.* (Consequence: the party is anchored and fed, the generals at hand — but the box is a stage, and Cecilia can visit it.)
> - **The lighting** — *She arrives at the lamps' lighting itself — the crowd's roar, the spectacle, the night's first wonder.* (Consequence: the entrance is magnificent, the town's first roar hers — and the walks begin their business before she is among them.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the paths, the box, or the lighting. The river hour comes. Hers to meet.)*
> - (T1) **Choose** — *the bright paths, the supper box, or the lighting. The shape of the night is the shape of the mistress.*
> - (T2) **Remembered consequence** — *whichever road, the lamps light — and the lighting is the thing; the manner is the means. The night is hers.*
> - (T3) **The road** — *the chosen road, carried to the household before the river hour; the night takes its order, in the manner Rose chose.*

Each road names the end. Each names it differently.)*

> - (T3) **The road** — *the chosen road, carried to the unmasking's edge; the end takes its order, in the manner Rose chose.*

scenes.synopsis: the night's ritual in flash structure — the dressing hour replayed at the salon's edge; the gown's attitude chosen; the weapons' hunt, dressed. (Turns: 21)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "Wednesday night. The defending is done, and Miss Hartwell goes after Cecilia's weapons — the flattery, the secrets, the remnants. She will walk into the enemy's salon, the counting-house's street, the town's whispering rooms, and the town will watch her go. The gown is armor for the hunt: the huntress, dressed, where the court can see her. **Editorial criterion: armor for the hunt — the woman who goes after the weapons, never the woman who waits for them.**"
>
> **A. The Thorn's Return** — crimson silk, the hunt declared. Motif: red roses embroidered at the hem, the thorns left on — defiance you can cut yourself on; the Hartwell oak in gold thread at the waist. Thread: **gold** (the oak) / **deep red** (the roses) / **crimson silk** (the standard, matched). Colorway: crimson + gold + green (the thorned stems). Accessories: the great gold oak brooch; her grandmother's pearls; the fan taken up — the salon's weapon, in her hand. Attitude: the hunt, declared — let them look, and let the looking cost them.
> **B. The Shadow** — charcoal silk, the weapons gathered unseen. Motif: a greyhound coursing in silver thread at the hem — the hunt, stated where only the looking will find it. Thread: **silver** (the hound) / **grey** (the coursing lines) / **charcoal silk** (the shadow, matched). Colorway: charcoal + silver + pearl. Accessories: her grandmother's pearls, doubled; the black fan, folded; no brooch — the severity is the point. Attitude: the huntress, unseen — nothing to accuse, everything to learn.
> **C. The Establishment** — black silk, Augusta's color, the untouchable. Motif: a single white rose at the breast — one bloom, nothing else; the skirt plain. Thread: **white** (the rose) / **black silk** (the night, matched). Colorway: black + white + pearl. Accessories: her grandmother's pearls; a black lace shawl for the street; no brooch — the mourning is worn before the fact. Attitude: the establishment, gone hunting — immovable, and dressed for it.
>
> *(The salon's edge, the night: her hand finds the gown's skirt — the silk, the armor — and the dressing hour comes back whole. The dressing room at the London house, the lamps lit, the direction undecided and waiting on the form. She dresses the way the week has dressed her: for the going after, against the waiting.)*
> (T1 · choice — the direction) *She commits: the Thorn's Return, the Shadow, or the Establishment — the attitude of the armor, remembered. The salon stands decided; this choice is the gown's alone. The hair, composed. The accessories, exact. The mirror, to be consulted briefly. **Direction.** Wednesday night — the lit house, the hunt's morning coming, the town's watching. Dress to go after, and to give the going its weight. **Editorial criterion.** Armor for the hunt — every choice must show the woman who goes after the weapons, never the woman who waits for them.*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE WEAPONS: which of Cecilia's weapons Rose takes up first. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Thursday evening, past six. The London house — the morning room, the lamps, the memorandum open on the week's gathering — and the decision sits in the middle of it: the weapons. The flattery has its address — the Thursday salon, the discoverer, the vanity cultivated. The secrets have their telling — the wages, the jewels, the lease, the sacred mornings. The remnants have their paper — the dead man's lease, the counting-house drafts, the credit named in ink. Three weapons, priced. The first taken is the question, and the question is the manner.)*
> *(She prices the means: flattery — cultivate the discoverer; the salon's mistress, flattered into talking, the court's texture drawn out of her vanity; the weapon Cecilia used on drawing rooms, turned on her own court; secrets — spend the whispers; the hired jewels, the advance wages, the dead man's lease, the sacred mornings — let the town hear what its new star is made of; the court's shine, bought, and bought things have bills; the remnants — follow Quill's paper; the counting-house, the drafts, the credit in ink; find the clerk's master and the money has a name Bell can print. Each road is hers. Each costs differently.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — The weapons:*
> - **Flattery** — *She cultivates the discoverer — the salon, the vanity; the flattery, turned on its maker.* (Consequence: the court's own salon talks — the texture comes freely, gift-wrapped in vanity; but flattery takes afternoons, and the discoverer may discover she is being used.)
> - **Secrets** — *She spends the whispers — the jewels, the wages, the lease; the town, told.* (Consequence: the court's shine tarnishes fast — the town loves a bought star unmasked; but whispers are not proof, and spending them spends her own credit too.)
> - **The remnants** — *She follows the paper — the drafts, the counting-house, the credit; the money, named.* (Consequence: the money gets its name — Bell prints what paper proves, and the machinery's purse is opened; but paper is patient and counting-houses are slower, and the court will feel the asking.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the flattery, the secrets, or the paper. The lamps burn. Hers to choose.)*
> - (T1) **Choose** — *flattery, secrets, or the remnants. The shape of the first weapon is the shape of the huntress.*
> - (T2) **Remembered consequence** — *whichever road, the weapons are gathered and the hunt is begun — and the choosing is the thing; the manner is the means. The weapons wait.*
> - (T3) **The road** — *the chosen road, carried into the lamps' light; the weapon takes its order, in the manner Rose chose.*
> *(The decision closes. The weapons have their first now — the huntress, given form. The lamps burn. The hunt goes on.)*

The trustees, the bank, the City — all have their own hours, and their own price for a mistress on their street.)*
> *(She prices the means: openly — walk it with Quill at her shoulder, the mistress on the money's street in daylight, the trustees' doors opened to her face; the City respects plain dealing, and the paper-man's shoulder is its own letter of credit; quietly — work it through Bell's contacts, the paper's street-friends, the coffee-house whispers, the clerks who talk to the Gazette's pencil; no mistress on the street, only the proprietor's listening; socially — send Laurent to the bankers' tables, the Comte's charm at the dinners and the wives' breakfasts, the ton's money talked loose over the port; the bankers' sons will tell a charming Frenchman what they would never tell a paper-man. Each road is hers. Each costs differently.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The City:*
> - **Openly** — *She walks it with Quill at her shoulder — the mistress, in daylight, on the money's street.* (Consequence: the City sees her take the street — the trustees respect a face at their doors, and the paper-man's shoulder opens them; but an open walk names her to the remnants, and the watching will report her steps by dinner.)
> - **Quietly** — *She works it through Bell's contacts — the paper's street-friends, the coffee-house whispers; no mistress on the street.* (Consequence: the chain is walked unseen — the clerks talk to the pencil, not the mistress; but second-hand paper comes slower, and Bell's contacts keep their own hours and their own prices.)
> - **Socially** — *She sends Laurent to the bankers' tables — the Comte's charm, the dinners, the wives' breakfasts; the ton's money, talked loose.* (Consequence: the bankers' sons tell a charming Frenchman what they hide from paper-men — the tables talk; but Laurent's pride is the old wound, and the bankers will want the Comte's own story in return for theirs.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the daylight, the whispers, or the charm. The street waits. Hers to choose.)*
> - (T1) **Choose** — *openly, quietly, or socially. The manner of the money's streets is the manner of the mistress.*

> **Occasion brief (published):** "Saturday morning. The trust's copy is whole, and Miss Hartwell walks the money's streets — the trustees' doors, the bank, the counting-houses — with Quill at her shoulder and the paper's terms in her reticule. The gown is armor for the money's road: the woman who walks it, dressed, where the City can see her. **Editorial criterion: armor for the money's streets — the woman who walks the money's road, never the woman who hides from it.**"
>
> **A. The Creditor's Black** — black silk, Augusta's color, the untouchable. Motif: the Hartwell oak in gold thread at the waist — the estate, stated where the money is walked. Thread: **gold** (the oak) / **black silk** (the creditor, matched). Colorway: black + gold + pearl. Accessories: her grandmother's pearls; the great gold oak brooch; the black pelisse for the street. Attitude: the creditor — the money's road, walked by its master.
> **B. The Clerk's Grey** — dove-grey silk, the paper's own color. Motif: a border of clerk's knotwork in silver thread at the hem — the counting-house's pattern, worn. Thread: **silver** (the knotwork) / **dove-grey silk** (the clerk, matched). Colorway: grey + silver + pearl. Accessories: her grandmother's pearls, single strand; the silver chatelaine; no brooch — the plainness is the point. Attitude: the paper's own — exact, plain, nothing to accuse.
> **C. The Iron Key** — charcoal silk, the strong room's color. Motif: a key in iron-grey thread at the hem — the lock, kept. Thread: **iron-grey** (the key) / **charcoal silk** (the iron, matched). Colorway: charcoal + iron + pearl. Accessories: her grandmother's pearls; the iron-grey shawl; no brooch — the severity is the keeping. Attitude: the lock — severity, and the keeping of it.
>

The dressing room at the London house, the morning's lamps, the direction undecided and waiting on the form. She dresses the way the week has dressed her: for the walking, against the hiding.)*

Dress to walk it, and to give the walking its weight. **Editorial criterion.** Armor for the money's streets — every choice must show the woman who walks the money's road, never the woman who hides from it.*

>

Thread: **gold** (the oak) / **black cloth** (the mistress, matched). Colorway: black + gold + pearl. Accessories: her grandmother's pearls; the great gold oak brooch at the throat; the black beaver hat. Attitude: the mistress — the Park's own rider, at the head of her field.

Thread: **silver** (the knotwork) / **dove-grey cloth** (the rider, matched). Colorway: grey + silver + pearl. Accessories: her grandmother's pearls, single strand; the plain black hat; no brooch — the plainness is the point. Attitude: the rider among riders — one of the field, not above it.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE TURNING: which of Cecilia's weapons Rose turns first — flattery, secrets, or the drawing room. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Wednesday night, past nine. The morning room — the lamps, the lists, the Harrow answer in the memorandum — and the decision sits in the middle of it: the turning. The war is resumed, and the terms are hers to name. Cecilia Vane fights with three weapons, and Rose Hartwell has studied them a season: the flattery that oils the ton's talk, the secrets placed like counters, the drawing rooms turned one by one. Tonight she lifts the first of them and turns it round.)*
> *(She prices the means: flattery — the ton's great vanity, the carrier of talk, courted and cultivated until it talks past caution; the seams of Cecilia's stories, shown by the very mouth that carried them; secrets — a truth, placed where it will travel, the ton's letters and breakfast tables; Cecilia's stories, answered at their roots by a truth no one can unplace; the drawing room — Cecilia's Thursday, turned whole; her own at-home declared on the same evening, and the town left to choose where it goes. Each road is hers. Each costs differently.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The Turning:*
> - **Flattery** — *She cultivates the ton's great vanity — the carrier of talk, courted until it talks.* (Consequence: the talker talks — flattered past caution, the very mouth that carried Cecilia's stories shows their seams; but vanity is a leaky vessel, and what it tells the town it will tell Cecilia too.)
> - **Secrets** — *She places a truth where it will travel — the ton's letters, the breakfast tables.* (Consequence: the truth travels — placed, not printed, it moves hand to hand and answers Cecilia's stories at their roots; but a placed truth can be re-placed, and the town will ask where she got it.)
> - **The drawing room** — *She turns Cecilia's Thursday whole — her own at-home, the same evening, and let the town choose.* (Consequence: the room turns — the ton's Thursday becomes hers for an evening, and the talk's direction reverses where the town can see it; but a room turned must be held, and Cecilia will come to take it back.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the vanity, the truth, or the room. The lamps burn. Hers to choose.)*
> - (T1) **Choose** — *flattery, secrets, or the drawing room. The first weapon turned is the war's new terms.*

scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "Thursday evening, the hour before her own Thursday. Miss Hartwell has declared her at-home on Cecilia's evening, and the town is choosing where to go. She dresses to turn the town — the gown as armor for the turning: defiance, stated where the ton can see it. **Editorial criterion: armor for the turning — defiance, never ornament.**"
>
> **A. The Open Red** — red silk, the Hartwell scarlet stated. Motif: the Hartwell oak in gold thread at the bodice — the house, where the town must look. Thread: **gold** (the oak) / **red silk** (the defiance, matched). Colorway: red + gold + pearl. scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE MONEY: how the money is named — plainly, gently, or without mercy. (Turns: 1 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Friday, the hour. The great rooms — the crowd, the light, Quill's last paper read — and the decision sits in the middle of it: the money. Each road is hers. Each costs differently.)*

> - **Plainly** — *The sums, the facts — the money named as money; no ornament, no cruelty.* (Consequence: the figures stand clean — the town cannot argue with arithmetic; but arithmetic does not bleed, and the town came to see blood.)
> - **Gently** — *The kindnesses named first — what the money did not buy, before what it bought.* (Consequence: the room softens — the refused and the paid, honored; but gentleness can be misread, and the town may call it weakness.)
> - **Without mercy** — *The winding's whole shape — every pound placed where the town can see it walk.* (Consequence: the war's price stands entire and unsoftened — the town sees all of it; but mercy withheld is remembered, and the town will remember who withheld it.)
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: plainly, gently, or without mercy. The figures are spoken. Hers to choose.)*
